result.summary:
The web rendering architecture holds up. Every (app) page is dynamic and per-user. Reads go through a request-scoped React cache(). Each read is settled into a designed partial-failure state. Dates format in an explicit en-US locale and the project's own timezone, so server and client render the same text. CLS measured 0 on all 30 cold routes. prefetch={false} demonstrably stops speculative fan-out (0 prefetch requests). Nothing here calls for Cache Components, PPR, 'use cache', workers or virtualization.

Highest-impact item, at the edge of this dimension: the web sign-out Server Actions call supabase.auth.signOut() with no scope. auth-js defaults that to 'global', which revokes the person's phone-collector session. The Account page promises the opposite ("Signing out here does not affect the app"). Uploads stop until the person signs in again. Records are not lost. The fix is one argument.

Second: the project and org loading.tsx files mount a new Suspense boundary on every tab switch. React 19.3's 300 ms reveal throttle then holds back pages that are ready in 60 ms. Measured: tab switches become usable at 327-345 ms, versus RSC plus about 20 ms for moves that don't remount the boundary. The user sees an empty card each time.

Third: every map page re-downloads, unzips and projects the whole package per render, and ships the full-resolution plan to client components. A reproducer on the real functions shows this is harmless at pilot size (real survey: 61 KB). It hits a cliff far below the API's 16 MiB ceiling: about 6 MB of plan JSON at an 832 KiB package, and an out-of-memory crash near 8 MiB.

The rest is lower impact:
- The Data table renders every record twice (15,213 DOM nodes, 2.2 MB of HTML for 500 rows).
- Mutations re-render the current page, often twice.
- A few independent reads run one after another.
- zod is bundled on every /o route because of one helper import.
- Compatibility code contradicts the no-legacy policy.

findings.trigger: The same person is signed in on the phone collector and on the web, for example a manager who also collects, or an observer who opens /o/<org>/collect or an invitation link. They press Sign out (header menu, Account > Security, or the delete-account page form), or 'Not you?' on /invite or /join.
findings.current_behavior: GoTrue logout runs with scope 'global', which revokes every refresh token the user has. The web clears its cookies and redirects to /sign-in. The phone keeps its current access token until it expires; its next refresh then fails and the collector is signed out. The person's other web browsers are signed out too. The mobile app itself deliberately signs out with scope 'local' (mobile-inventory map, sign-out.tsx).
findings.consequence: The web states something false about the record pipeline. The phone stops uploading until the observer signs in again, possibly in the field. Records stay on the device (owner_scope partition), so this is blocked sync and a broken promise, not record loss. The code comment shows the intent was this browser only.
findings.smallest_fix: Pass { scope: 'local' } to supabase.auth.signOut() in lib/auth/actions.ts:138 and features/auth/actions.ts:127. If 'sign out everywhere' is ever wanted, make it a separate, explicitly worded control.
findings.can_delete: Nothing.
findings.guarantee_to_keep: Sign-out still clears this browser's Supabase and flow cookies and redirects. Account deletion keeps its local sign-out plus cookie wipe.
findings.verification_scenario: Sign in as the same user in two browser contexts (or web plus simulator). Sign out in context A. In context B, call supabase.auth.refreshSession() (or wait past token expiry): B must stay signed in and the collector must still upload. The existing zones-account e2e (same-context tabs) must still see 'you were signed out' because the cookies are shared.
findings.journey: Account / any workspace header -> Sign out; Invite/Join -> Not you?

findings.trigger: Clicking any project tab (Overview, Data, Sites, Forms, Reports, QGIS, Team, Settings) or org tab, because the child segment under the layout changes.
findings.current_behavior:
Next mounts a new keyed Suspense boundary for the new child segment and shows ProjectLoading. That is a bordered Island whose rows stay at opacity 0 until 400 ms, and the page header disappears with the old page. When the server payload arrives, React's retry throttle holds the reveal until 300 ms after the fallback committed. Measured soft navigations, with the API on localhost:
- data->sites: RSC done 60 ms, usable 332 ms
- site/zones->forms: RSC 63 ms, usable 331 ms
- overview->data: RSC 117 ms, usable 345 ms

Moves that keep the [project] child segment (no new boundary) are usable about 20 ms after the RSC finishes: sites->site 90 -> 112 ms, data->observation 70 -> 88 ms.
findings.consequence: Every tab switch gains about 200-270 ms at lab speed and flashes an empty card. This is the opposite of the file's stated intent. The cost shrinks only when the server is slower than 300 ms.
findings.smallest_fix: Delete both loading.tsx files. Wrap {children} in one persistent <Suspense fallback={<same Island/ScreenState>}> inside p/[project]/layout.tsx:33 and (org)/layout.tsx:20. Cold loads still stream the skeleton. Tab switches become transitions over an already-revealed boundary, so the old page stays until the new one is ready and nothing is throttled. Optionally add a pending mark to InkTabs with next/link useLinkStatus (bundled docs 01-app/01-getting-started/04-linking-and-navigating.md:233). Not verified by running.
findings.can_delete: The two loading.tsx files.
findings.guarantee_to_keep: A skeleton during cold loads, prefetch={false}, the error.tsx boundaries, and Overview's inner Coverage Suspense.
findings.verification_scenario: Rerun scratchpad/runtime/warmnav.cjs. Tab switches should be usable at about RSC total + 20 ms (for example data->sites near 80 ms, not 332 ms). A performance trace should have no frame without the page header. cold.json FCP for project routes should be unchanged (about 64-76 ms).

findings.trigger: Any navigation to Overview, Data, Observation, Sites, Site, Zones, the zone draft editor or publish, package inspect, or the form editor. warm-nav.json shows downloadPackageArchive on every soft navigation to these pages. The scaling trigger is a manager uploading a denser QGIS drawing that the API accepts.
findings.current_behavior:
Nothing is reused across navigations. Each render downloads the archive from the API, runs unzipSync and JSON.parse synchronously on the Node event loop, projects every vertex to full-precision plan units, and serializes the ProjectedSite to client components (DataScreen, CoverageIsland, SiteScreen, and SitesScreen for up to 6 sites) in addition to the SVG. Lab archives cost 7-13 ms.

The reproducer (scratchpad/repro/siteplan-cost.mjs) runs the real readPackageArchive, packageSiteCollection and projectSite:
- Fall Creek's real layers, 10 KiB zip: 3 ms; 61 KiB projected JSON
- 832 KiB zip: 85 ms CPU; 5.6 MB projected JSON
- 7.9 MiB zip: 811 ms CPU; 55 MB projected JSON; process at 1.36 GB RSS
- next size up: Node crashed out of memory

The real survey drawings (Ithaca_QGIS/Drawings, 1,553 vertices) project to about 61 KB, so the pilot is far from the cliff.
findings.consequence: At pilot scale there is no harm. A package of about 1 MiB would put about 6 MB of plan JSON plus SVG into each map page, multiplied up to 6 times on Sites. Around 8 MiB, each plan blocks the function for about a second and the page risks running out of memory. That site's web pages would become unusable while the API still calls the package ready.
findings.smallest_fix: Add a byte budget in getSitePlan and getEditorBase, checking bytes.length before unzipSync. Over budget, return null so the existing planNote path says the plan is too detailed to draw on the web and to open it in QGIS. State the same limit once as an API preparation check. Round projected coordinates (for example 2 decimals in plan units) to roughly halve the payload. Only after real package sizes show a need, add a process-level cache of projected plans keyed by immutable package_id. Cache Components or 'use cache' are not justified for this.
findings.can_delete: Nothing.
findings.guarantee_to_keep: Each plan is still read through the viewer's own authorized archive request, keeps its historical binding (the record's own package version), and keeps the honest planNote when it cannot be drawn.
findings.verification_scenario: Unit test: an archive over the budget makes getSitePlan return null without calling unzipSync, and the Data, Site and Sites pages show the note. Rerun siteplan-cost.mjs and compare projected JSON size after rounding. Re-measure cold.json 'zones' and 'sites' document sizes.
findings.journey: Site plans across review pages
findings.evidence_needed: Real package sizes from the pilot and other QGIS projects, and hosted function memory and time per map page.

result.assessment_markdown:
## How a workspace page gets from navigation to usable content (verified in code)

1. **Proxy.** `proxy.ts:13-49` runs on every matched request, including RSC and Server Action POSTs. It calls `getClaims()`, which is local: the project signs ES256 (`docs/Supabase-Setup.md:11`) and auth-js keeps the JWKS cache module-global (`GoTrueClient.js:49-69`). A signed-out request to a protected path redirects to `/sign-in?next=`. Matched responses get `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.
2. **(app) layout.** `(app)/layout.tsx:28` awaits `getWorkspace()`: `session()` (getClaims + getSession), then `GET /v1/me`. It never throws. The whole index goes to `WorkspaceProvider`. This blocks all `(app)` HTML. Measured TTFB is 25-57 ms locally. It is needed for slug-to-ID resolution and roles, so the block is justified.
3. **Org layout and project layout.** `[org]/layout.tsx:20-38` and `p/[project]/layout.tsx:23-26` add cache hits, `notFound()` and the observer redirect. Per the bundled docs (`06-fetching-data.md:455`), layouts and pages render in parallel, so page reads start at the same time.
4. **Page.** Each page runs `resolveProject` (a cache hit), then its own waves of reads. Every read is `settle()`d into a `Result`, and a failed read renders a designed `LoadFailure`, never an empty list.
5. **Hand-off.** Props are serialized to `'use client'` screens, then streamed through the project `loading.tsx` Suspense, then hydrated.

On soft navigations only the changed segments render, but every page still pays one `/v1/me` call (`get_identity` appears in every warm-nav list). Back and forward are served from the router cache in 12-20 ms with no requests.

## Route table

| Route | navigation → usable path | blocking reads (seq / ∥) | measured cost (prod build, local API, no throttle) | boundary coverage | recommended bounded change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| /sign-in, sign-up, verify, forgot, reset | proxy → page (no API) | none | TTFB 11.5, LCP 52 ms, doc 33 KB | global-error, root not-found | none |
| /o | proxy → identity → 307 to remembered or only project | identity | 307 at 40-58 ms; overview usable at 324 ms | global-error | none |
| /o/[org] | identity → readOrg → listOrgProjects → ∥ listSites (≤12) | 3 seq | TTFB 25, docEnd 69, LCP 140 | (org)/loading, [org]/error, not-found | R2 (persistent Suspense) |
| members, org settings | identity → readOrg → one ∥ wave | 2 | lab user had no access: LCP 68-72 | same | none |
| Overview | identity → ∥[P, S, S→N×listPackages, forms, obs500] → ∥[today, 7d] → ∥ getPackage(blocked) → Suspense Coverage ∥[summary, archive] | 4-5 seq | 10 sites: docEnd 241, LCP 324, 19 calls. 30 sites/520 obs: 37 calls, docEnd 528, LCP 488, usable 541 | project loading + error, inner Suspense | R6: counts off P; coverage reads start in wave 1 |
| Data | identity → ∥[P, S] → (listPackages if ?version) → ∥[obs500, ≤3 summaries] → form versions → archive | 4-5 | 8 rows: docEnd 124, LCP 216. 500 rows: docEnd 581, LCP 840, 15,213 DOM, 2.2 MB HTML, 114 ms long task; soft nav ~700 ms | project | R4 (one DOM structure); archive ∥ form versions |
| data/[observation] | identity → getObservation → ∥[P, archive, S] | 3 | docEnd 86, LCP 180; soft 88-105 | project | R6: P, S together with getObservation |
| forms, forms/versions | identity → ∥[forms, S, P] | 2 | lab API 500, failure path only (LCP 152-156); soft zones→forms usable 331 vs RSC 63 | project | R2 |
| forms/versions/[v] (editor) | identity → getFormVersion → ∥[forms, S] → base version → archive | 5 | not measurable (lab 500) | project | R6 (2 waves), R5 (Save) |

CLS was 0.000 on all 30 cold routes, and there were no console or page errors.

## Specific questions

- **Does getWorkspace block every child, and what loading/Suspense exists?** Yes, by design. Only two segment loading files exist (project, org) plus Overview's Coverage Suspense. They flush a skeleton on cold loads, but on soft navigations they cost ≥300 ms per tab switch (R2).
- **Archives during render (R3).** Triggered on Overview coverage, Data, observation detail, Sites (×6), Site, Zones, the zone editor and publish, package inspect, the form editor, and `loadSitePlanAction`. Repeated on every navigation. Synchronous unzip on the event loop. Projected JSON is about 6-7× the zip. Fine at pilot scale (real survey: 61 KB); a cliff near 1-8 MiB.
- **Large props.**
  - Data: 500 rows → 418.6 KB RSC and 2.2 MB HTML; most of the HTML is the doubled DOM (R4).
  - Reports: 288 KB HTML for 520 observations.
  - The workspace index and the timezone list are small: there is no evidence they matter.
- **Client graph.**
  - cmdk is about 20 KB raw: keep it eager.
  - Radix is shared by the dialogs.
  - zod (73 KB br) reaches 10 routes only through LoadFailure (R7).
  - supabase-js is needed only when the user clicks export on Data, Site or QGIS.
  - Lazy-loading CommandPalette would only delay the first ⌘K; not worth it.
- **prefetch={false}.** Justified. The overview has 31 workspace links, and measured prefetch requests are 0. With the default ("auto") prefetch, each visible link would still hit the server (proxy, layouts, /v1/me) only to fetch a loading shell, because dynamic data is never prefetched. The navigation latency people feel comes from R2, not from the missing prefetch.
- **revalidatePath breadth.** With `fetch` no-store and no Data Cache, revalidation re-renders the current page and purges the router cache; it invalidates nothing on the server.
  - `/o` layout revalidation after org, team, settings and account changes is correct, because the header and switchers read the workspace index.
  - Revalidating the project layout on every form Save is waste, and three flows refresh twice (R5).
  - No client state is lost: the editor's key is stable and its state comes from initial props.
- **Boundaries.**
  - Every project page sits under `p/[project]/error.tsx`.
  - Org pages sit under `[org]/error.tsx` and `not-found.tsx`.
  - `notFound()` thrown in the project layout lands on the org not-found (the shell stays). Thrown in the org layout, it lands on the root not-found (public header). Acceptable.
  - `/account`, `/o`, `/collect` and the auth pages rely on global-error, but they catch API failures themselves.
  - Latent issue, not a finding: `apiRequestError` (`errors.ts:284-291`) turns any TypeError reaching `settle()` into "DECA Mark cannot be reached". Probing odd archives (scratchpad/repro/odd-package.mjs) found no reachable case.
- **Hydration and theme.**
  - Every formatter fixes `en-US` and an explicit timezone (`lib/time.ts:108-111`, `labels.ts:56`), and `nowIso` comes from the server, so server and client render the same text.
  - `InvitationCard` and `ErrorView` use the browser's timezone, but render only after an action or effect.
  - The head `THEME_SCRIPT` plus `suppressHydrationWarning` on `<html>` gives no flash; CLS was 0.
- **Deep links, refresh, back/forward.**
  - Data filters live in the URL (`router.push`, so Back undoes them); search text via debounced `replaceState` that keeps `history.state`.
  - Reports, QGIS and Overview use `router.replace`.
  - The leave guard copies the router's history entry, so Back is held without breaking the router.
  - Back is served from the router cache. The zone editor re-reads its draft before saving, so a page restored from history cannot overwrite a newer draft.
- **Cache Components / PPR / 'use cache'** (`cacheComponents:false`, `config-shared.js:135`). No justified benefit on any route.
  - Every route is per-user and authorized per request.
  - A static shell would only show empty chrome.
  - Identity is one fast call that must stay fresh for role changes.
  - The only immutable, repeated data is the package plan. The byte guard in R3 is the bounded fix; caching it is premature until real package sizes show a need.
justified_choices: prefetch={false} on workspace links: 0 measured prefetch RSC requests across 31 overview links. It protects the API from per-link proxy plus /v1/me fan-out, and with dynamic routes the default would only have prefetched a loading shell anyway.
One getWorkspace per request through React cache(), and getWorkspace never throws; layouts and pages share one /v1/me call.
settle()/Result with LoadFailure: one failed read renders a designed partial state, and a failed fetch is never an empty list (honesty rule).
Every Intl formatter fixes locale en-US and an explicit project timezone, and nowIso is computed on the server, so SSR and hydration produce identical text.
Head THEME_SCRIPT plus suppressHydrationWarning only on <html>, with data-platform for shortcut hints: no theme flash; CLS 0 on all 30 measured routes.
Overview's Coverage section in its own Suspense, so the package archive does not block the rest of the Overview.
Package uploads, exports and downloads go browser -> API directly (bodies up to 24 MiB) instead of through Server Actions (2 MB limit).
Data view state lives in the URL (router.push per filter, debounced replaceState for search that preserves history.state): deep links, refresh and Back all work.
The observation detail page draws the record's own package version (historical binding), not today's map.
Cache-Control private, no-store and Referrer-Policy no-referrer on all proxied responses; the service worker never stores authenticated responses or RSC payloads.
No Cache Components, PPR or 'use cache': every route is per-user, and nothing measured needs them.
ES256 sign-in with a module-global JWKS cache: getClaims in the proxy and on the server verifies locally, with no auth round trip per request.

result.summary:
The data and caching layer is mostly sound. Nothing is cached on the server: API fetches use `no-store`, and React `cache()` only lasts for one request. There is no optimistic UI, so a refresh can never bring old data back. The service worker stores only public files. The WorkspaceProvider sends the viewer only their own data. Manager-only pages check the role before they read, and the database functions I sampled enforce membership and role again. The counts say when they come from the newest 500. Signing out writes cookies inside a Server Action, and in Next 16.2.7 that clears both the client router cache and the back/forward cache. The packagePlans memo is keyed by user, project and package.

There are three material defects, all reachable by ordinary use or a plain phishing link:
(1) The web Sign out uses Supabase's default global scope. It ends the person's collector session on every device, while the Account page says signing out "does not affect the app".
(2) The code assumes every Server Action call resolves to a typed result. A dropped connection, a session that ended (the proxy redirects action POSTs with 307), or a version mismatch after a deploy makes the call reject instead. In the form editor and the settings screens that rejection reaches the error boundary, so the editor unmounts and unsaved form edits are lost behind "Your records remain available". Some other call sites just fail with no message.
(3) `safeNext` checks for "//" before the URL is normalised, so a link like `/sign-in?next=/a/..//evil.com` sends the person to an outside site right after a real sign-in. I reproduced this with the real function.

Two low findings complete the list. The installed web app shows the marketing page offline. Browser-direct uploads and exports, and the palette's recent places, ignore which account the tab belongs to. All fixes are a few lines each. Nothing here calls for adding caching.

findings.current_behavior: The Server Action promise rejects: the fetch throws, or the proxy 307s the POST to /sign-in and the forwarded action comes back as '{}' JSON, which is not an RSC response. The rejection happens inside a useTransition action, so React 19.2.4 throws it to the project error boundary. DraftEditorScreen unmounts, the leave guard goes with it, and ErrorView says 'Something went wrong. Your records remain available.' Its Try again rebuilds the editor from server props, so the edits are gone. The typed 'Nothing was saved. Sign in to continue.' path in forms/actions.ts:33-43 is never reached when the session has ended. In the site dialogs and in 'Show the next 500' the rejection is unhandled, and the button returns to normal with no message.
findings.consequence: The manager loses form-draft work through ordinary network or session events, and the page gives no true reason. This breaks the 'a failed read/write says what did not happen' rule, and the zone editor already handles the same cases properly.
findings.smallest_fix: Add one small helper, e.g. settleAction(promise, nothing), that turns a rejection into {status:'failed', message: UNCONFIRMED_CHANGE_COPY} (lib/api/errors.ts:293). Use it at the ~13 call sites listed. In proxy.ts, skip the sign-in redirect for non-GET/HEAD requests (or requests with a next-action header), so the action itself answers with its typed sign-in failure; ideally reword it as 'Sign in again in another tab, then save', as save-queue.ts:409 does. Keep the typed failures, the 'may have saved' honesty, the leave guard and the editor's in-memory state. Nothing needs deleting.
findings.guarantee_to_keep: Protected document and RSC GETs still redirect to /sign-in?next=; the API still refuses unauthenticated writes; an unconfirmed write is never reported as success.
findings.verification_scenario: Playwright with manager storage state: open forms/versions/<draft>, change a question's wording, call context.setOffline(true), click Save draft. Today ErrorView appears and, back online, the old wording returns. After the fix an attention Note with the unconfirmed copy appears, the edited wording is still in the fields, and going back online and pressing Save draft saves it. Repeat by signing out in a second page of the same context instead of going offline.

justified_choices: No server data cache: API fetches use cache:'no-store' (web/src/lib/api/client.ts:57) and React cache() only removes duplicate reads within one request (lib/api/workspace.ts:55-62). No 'use cache', unstable_cache or staleTimes anywhere. For authenticated research data this is the right default, and it means a refresh always shows the API's current state.

Sign-out and sign-in run as Server Actions that write cookies. In Next 16.2.7 any cookie set/delete in an action marks ActionDidRevalidateStaticAndDynamic (server/web/spec-extension/adapters/request-cookies.js:111-116), and the client then calls invalidateBfCache and invalidateEntirePrefetchCache (server-action-reducer.js:192-209; docs 01-app/04-glossary.md:45). So Back after sign-out refetches and the proxy redirects; documents are also private, no-store (proxy.ts:47).

The WorkspaceProvider index holds only the viewer's own userId, name, email and their orgs, projects and roles (lib/workspace/types.ts:27-52, build.ts:37-63); no other members, no join codes, no tokens.

Invitation secrets: lists never carry them (backend invitation_schemas.py:42-59; token and code only on InvitationCreated, shown once). The link secret lives in the URL fragment, then in this tab's sessionStorage, and is removed from the address bar (features/auth/InviteScreen.tsx:76-85); no-referrer is set on the proxy response and on the invite and join pages.

Pages check the role before reading: Members, Org settings, Team, Project settings and Form publish all check abilities before calling manager-only endpoints (e.g. team/page.tsx:32-49, (org)/members/page.tsx:24-32). The API/DB enforces this again for client-supplied ids: change_org_member, change_project_member and create_invitation check has_org_role/has_project_role (supabase baseline.sql:300-336,467-490), and require_manager is used in services/tenancy.py:53,59 and services/invitations.py:132,137.

packagePlans memo is keyed userId:projectId:packageId over immutable packages (features/data/plans.ts:3-17), so sign-out or an account change cannot leak a plan; DataMap ignores late responses with a request token (DataMap.tsx:119-187).

The service worker caches only '/', /icons/* and /_next/static/*, after checking each response (service-worker.js:8-41); it skips RSC and Authorization requests (:82) and prewarms with credentials:'omit'. Nothing authenticated is cached.

Counts are honest about the 500 cap: Data countLine/subsetNote; the Export dialog says the search is not applied (ExportObservations.tsx:132-136); Reports say 'counted from the newest N' (ReportsScreen.tsx:316,335-353); Overview's Last received says it is read from the newest N (FieldReturnIsland.tsx:36-37,89); org rows say 'skipped' or 'failed', never zero (org/projects/rows.ts:7-58). Table, map, summary and export all use the same server-applied filters (data/page.tsx:70-111; reports/page.tsx:64-79).
No optimistic UI (no useOptimistic), so no rollback paths are needed; mutations return typed results and revalidate.
fm-place cookie holds a path only and is re-validated against the new account's index (lib/workspace/home.ts:19-44), so a second account is never routed into the first account's project.

Double submit: busy Buttons cancel the click with preventDefault (components/contour/Button.tsx:116-118), which also blocks implicit Enter submission; the package upload and zone StartDraft carry request ids.

keep_despite_complex.item: Zone draft autosave queue and account fence (features/zones/editor/useDraftSaving.ts, save-queue.ts, lib/api/zones-browser.ts)
keep_despite_complex.why: It is the only web path that persists work continuously. If-Match, one PUT in flight, abort on fence, a signed-out pause that resumes when auth-js recovers on visibility (GoTrueClient _recoverAndRefresh emits SIGNED_IN), and the fence purging another account's edits are each exercised in e2e (zones-account.spec.ts:69,114; zones-network). It is also the model WDI-1 and WDI-5 should copy.

keep_despite_complex.item: Package upload idempotent resend (features/packages/UploadStep.tsx:252-263, 399-470)
keep_despite_complex.why: Resending the same request_id and expected_current_package_id after an unknown answer is what prevents a second map version or an overwrite of a newer map after a lost response.

keep_despite_complex.item: Per-request role check plus the API/DB check (lib/workspace/access.ts used on pages, DB functions enforce)
keep_despite_complex.why: It looks redundant, but the page check keeps manager-only endpoints from being called (web/AGENTS.md:25), and the DB check is the real authorisation for ids that come from the client.

keep_despite_complex.item: Draft form editor ETag and conflict copy (DraftEditorScreen.tsx:90-183, features/forms/result.ts:30-42)
keep_despite_complex.why: Saving with If-Match and keeping the editor's text on 409/412/428 is correct. Only the transport-failure path (WDI-1) is missing.

not_covered: Nothing was run: the WDI-1 boundary path, the WDI-3 hard redirect and the WDI-2 device sign-out are traced in installed Next 16.2.7, React 19.2.4 and auth-js 2.117.2 source, not exercised in a browser or simulator.

Hosted Supabase Auth settings (refresh-token rotation and reuse interval, session time-box or inactivity timeout, whether a password change revokes other sessions) decide how often sessions end mid-edit; they were not inspected.
Safari/iPad back/forward cache behaviour for private, no-store documents was not checked; the analysis relies on sign-out being a client-side navigation that purges Next's own caches.

Backend authorization was sampled (organizations, tenancy members, invitations, project and org patch), not audited route by route; observation RLS was taken from the 2026-10-17 migration evidence in the product map.

Archive download and projection cost per render and server-side plan memoisation belong to the rendering/performance dimension (see the web-rendering notes). No server caching of research data is recommended here; if it is ever added, the only safe key is an immutable package id, read after the user's own authorised package read.

No CSP or frame-ancestors header is set (proxy.ts:47-48 sets only Cache-Control and Referrer-Policy). Clickjacking of signed-in actions is largely blocked by SameSite=Lax session cookies in cross-site frames; noted as hardening, not a finding.
Mobile-side handling after WDI-2's revocation (upload pause UX, sign-in prompt) is left to the mobile audit.
result.assessment_markdown:
## Data classes: source, caches, scope, freshness, failure

| Data class | Authoritative source | Cache layers that actually hold it | Identity / scope key | Freshness & invalidation | Failure · logout · account change · permission change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Workspace index / me | `GET /v1/me` + Supabase claims (`getWorkspace`, lib/api/workspace.ts:71) | React `cache()` per request; `(app)` layout → `WorkspaceProvider` context (layout kept across soft navigations); RSC payload in router back/forward cache; localStorage `fm.palette.recent` (names + role labels); cookie `fm-place` (path only, 1 year) | session cookie `sub`; recents unkeyed; `fm-place` unkeyed but re-checked by `homeFor` | Server: every request. Client context: only on `revalidatePath("/o","layout")` (org/team/settings/account/invite actions), `router.refresh`, reload | Failure → `status:"unavailable"` → LoadFailure (never throws). Logout → cookie write purges router cache and back/forward cache; `(app)` subtree unmounts; recents and `fm-place` survive (filtered / re-checked). Account change in another tab → tab keeps the old context until it navigates; actions run as the new account. Permission change → next page request re-reads; tabs/menus stale until then (UI only) |
| Project (P) | `GET /v1/projects/{id}` | `cache()` per request; RSC back/forward; name also in the index | project id found from slug/code in the index | Re-read on every navigation (`staleTimes.dynamic` 0, config-shared.js:242); settings actions revalidate `/o` layout | LoadFailure; `notFound` when not in the index |
| Sites (S) | `GET …/sites` (exact `observation_count`) | `cache()` per request; RSC back/forward | project | Every navigation; site actions `revalidatePath(project,"layout")` | LoadFailure; site edit is last-writer-wins (no ETag), acceptable for one manager |
| Packages + plans | package list/detail, archive → server unzip + projection per render (`getSitePlan` workspace.ts:243) | `cache()` per request; browser `packagePlans` LRU of 8 (Data map only); downloads checked against the ETag SHA-256 | `userId:projectId:packageId` (immutable) | Server: per request. Memo never stale (packages immutable). Upload → `packageUploaded` revalidation + `router.refresh` | planNote / LoadFailure. Memo cleared only by the zone fence, and safe because it is keyed. Upload is not bound to the page's account (WDI-5) |
| Forms / versions | form version resources with ETag | `cache()` per request; editor `raw/saved/etag` in memory only (no autosave, no storage) | version code + ETag | Save with If-Match; every form action revalidates the project layout; conflict → open latest in a new tab | Typed failures keep the edits; a transport failure or ended session → error boundary, edits lost (WDI-1) |
| Observations list | `GET …/observations` (newest 500 + `total_matching` + cursor) | `cache()` per request; `DataScreen` state, more pages added by `loadObservationsAction`; component key = view + `generated_at` | filters in the URL, cursor tied to them | New server render per filter change; Refresh = `router.refresh`; no background polling | RLS limits observers to their own records. "Show the next 500" fails with no message on transport errors (WDI-1) |
| Observation detail | `GET …/observations/{id}` | `cache()` per request | UUID + project | Every navigation | 404 → `notFound` |
| Summaries / coverage | summarize endpoint (server counts every match) | `cache()` per request; Overview coverage behind Suspense | same filters as the list | Every navigation | Failure named, never shown as zero |
| Reports | summary + newest 500 (same filters) | `cache()` per request; printed with `window.print` | URL `site/round/from/to` | Every navigation | Says "counted from the newest N" |
| Exports / downloads | `GET …/export` ZIP (≤10,000), archive, zones (browser → API) | none (Blob saved to disk) | bearer token of whoever is signed in at click time | Made at click time | Typed failure note; over 10,000 refused before sending; not bound to the page's account (WDI-5) |
| Team / invitations | members and invitations endpoints (manager-only, role checked first) | `cache()` per request; the new invitation's token and code exist only in dialog memory, shown once | project/org id from the client; API/DB enforce | Invitations revalidate `/team`; role/member changes revalidate `/o` layout | Secrets never in lists; refusals typed |
| Zone drafts | draft resource with revision/ETag (zones-browser.ts) | editor reducer + save queue in memory; sessionStorage `zone-publish:<draft>:<rev>` request id | `userId:projectId:draftId`; `expectUser` fence | Autosave 1.5 s (at most 10 s), flush on hide/blur; draft read again on mount; 409/412 pause with a choice | Signed out → pause, resumes on SIGNED_IN; another account → fence and purge; offline flag |
| Public shell | build output | SW `decamark-public-<build>`: `/`, `/icons/*`, `/_next/static/*` | none (public) | New cache per build; old ones deleted on activate | Offline `/o` → landing page (WDI-4) |

## Identity / caching risks
1. **Global sign-out (WDI-2):** web Sign out and "Not you?" end the person's sessions on every device, including the collector; the Account page copy says otherwise.
2. **Ended session or dropped connection during a Server Action (WDI-1):** the proxy 307s action POSTs. Rejected actions are not caught in transitions, so unsaved form-editor and settings input is lost behind a generic error.
3. **Open redirect (WDI-3):** `safeNext` returns `//host` for paths that normalise to it. This is the only external-navigation hole found.
4. **Account binding (WDI-5):** only the zone editor and account deletion check that the signed-in account is the page's. Upload, import, export and downloads, plus the palette recents, do not.
5. **Stale shell after another manager changes your role:** `WorkspaceProvider` and the project tabs are layout state and are not refetched on soft navigation. This affects controls only; every page and every API call re-checks. Acceptable.
6. **Back button after sign-out:** safe in Next 16.2.7, because cookie writes in the sign-out action purge the router's back/forward cache and documents are `private, no-store`.
7. **Service worker:** nothing authenticated is cached. The offline `/o` fallback to the marketing page is misleading, not harmful (WDI-4). The legacy `fieldmaps-*` cache names are pre-launch compatibility code and can be deleted.
8. **Caching research data:** do not add any. If plan projection cost is ever addressed, the only safe server memo key is an immutable package id, used after the user's own authorised package read. Measure first.

results.checked: Opened every cited site. DraftEditorScreen save (:143-183) and startFromThis (:196-209), PublishScreen :79, RetireDialog :37, DiscardDialog :41, NewFormDialog :79, FormVersionsScreen :100, org SettingsScreen :98, TransferOwnership :58, CreateProjectDialog :104 and project-settings SettingsScreen :120 all call start(async () => { await xAction(...) }) from useTransition with no try/catch. EditSiteDialog :74-87, CreateSiteDialog :92-116 and DataScreen.loadMore :186-206 use try/finally with no catch, so the rejection is an unhandled promise rejection and the busy flag resets with no message. In React 19.2.4, chainThenableValue (react-dom-client.development.js:5873) and updateTransition (:9022, useThenable) rethrow a rejected async transition at render. A react-test-renderer@19.2.4 reproducer (scratchpad/repro/v/transition-reject.cjs) showed the nearest error boundary rendering on rejection, and the component staying mounted with try/catch. In Next 16.2.7, server-action-reducer.js:69-73 does the POST fetch, :111-121 throws 'An unexpected response was received from the server.' for a non-RSC reply without x-action-redirect, and :302-305 calls reject(e). The only boundaries are app/(app)/o/[org]/p/[project]/error.tsx, [org]/error.tsx and global-error.tsx; ErrorView shows 'Something went wrong.' / 'Your records remain available.' and Try again (unstable_retry) remounts from server props. The forms feature has no autosave or storage, and the service worker (service-worker.js:82) ignores non-GET, so an offline POST really rejects. proxy.ts:17,33-43 issues NextResponse.redirect (default 307, response.js:99) for every method under /o and /account. action-handler.js:456-466 and :127-206 forward the action to a worker that has it, with redirect:'manual', and a non-RSC result becomes '{}' JSON. That session-ended chain is code-traced only, not run. Correct patterns confirmed at zones/StartDraft.tsx:64-75, DiscardDraft.tsx:58-75, DataMap.tsx:165-187 and zones/editor/save-queue.ts:409. No code or test already guards the form editor. WDI-3 and WDI-2 are separate findings.
results.correction: The core claim holds: a rejected Server Action inside start(async ...) throws to the project error boundary and discards unsaved form-editor edits, and the try/finally sites fail silently. Three corrections. (1) Severity is medium, not high. The loss is limited to edits since the last manual Save, the trigger is transient (offline at the moment of Save, session ended), nothing server-side is corrupted, and the manager can redo the edits. (2) The smallest_fix is wrong about the copy. If proxy.ts merely stops redirecting non-GET requests, a signed-out action reaches resolveProject, then getWorkspace 'unauthenticated', then workspaceError, which builds an ApiError with no status. failedChange then calls failedWrite, and wasRefused(status undefined) is false, so the message is UNCONFIRMED_CHANGE_COPY ('could not confirm the change. Reload the page...'), not 'Nothing was saved. Sign in to continue.'. That copy only appears on a real API 401 with a status. The copy needs its own sign-in wording such as save-queue.ts:409's 'Sign in again in another tab, then come back to save', and 'Reload the page' is bad advice here because a document GET redirects to sign-in and drops the edits. (3) The ~13 call sites count is roughly right (14 by my count). The settleAction helper plus the proxy tweak is a sound minimal design. The offline and 5xx/413 triggers are the strongest evidence. The session-ended chain through the forwarded-action '{}' response is only code-traced.

results.checked: web/src/lib/auth/actions.ts:136-146 signOut calls supabase.auth.signOut() with no scope (:138), and features/auth/actions.ts:124-133 switchAccount does the same (:127). The installed @supabase/auth-js 2.117.2 GoTrueClient.js:3417 defaults to scope 'global', and its doc comment at :3384-3398 says this 'signs the user out of every device'. @supabase/ssr 0.12.7 does not override the scope. The only web caller using 'local' is account deletion (features/account/actions.ts:103). The copy SecurityIsland.tsx:23 ('Signing out here does not affect the app...') contradicts this. Callers confirmed: SecurityIsland.tsx:50, AccountMenu.tsx:47,120 and DeleteAccount.tsx:150, the last in the deletion-finishing state where global is harmless. Mobile deliberately uses scope 'local' (provider.tsx:89,129; mobile/PLAN.md:242,264). PLAN.md:126 names 'global sign-out' as a cause of supabase-js deleting the session. session-retention.ts:19-24 keeps the account and nulls the session on an unexpected SIGNED_OUT. gate.tsx decideGate sets signedIn = session || cachedAccount and authOpen = !session, so the app stays in the 'app' route. SessionBanner and ResumeUploadsNote show 'Sign in to resume uploads'. The backend verifies JWTs locally via JwksVerifier (backend/src/fieldmaps_api/auth.py), so the phone keeps working until its access token expires (about 1 h). Not run end to end (no servers or devices).
results.correction: The core claim is confirmed: web Sign out and 'Not you?' revoke every session for that user, which contradicts the Account page footnote. The consequence is overstated. Collection is not blocked: the cached account keeps the gate on the app route, and records and local collection continue. What stops is uploads, after the access token lapses (about 1 h) and the refresh fails. The app shows 'Sign in to resume uploads', and the fix is the person re-entering their password on the device, so it is recoverable and loses nothing. Severity is medium, not high. It is reachable by an ordinary user with one account on web and phone, and by the shared-laptop 'Not you?' case. The two-line fix ({ scope: 'local' } at lib/auth/actions.ts:138 and features/auth/actions.ts:127) is correct and is not a backward-compatibility request.

results.checked: I ran the real safeNext (web/src/lib/auth/navigation.ts via node --experimental-strip-types). One pass does return '//evil.com' for '/a/..//evil.com', '/.//evil.com' and '/%2e%2e//evil.com', and '//evil.com/x' for '/o/..//evil.com/x'. I then traced every sink that reaches redirect(). Each auth page runs safeNext first (sign-in/page.tsx:19, sign-up:19, verify:23, forgot-password:25, reset-password:53) and passes the result as the hidden input name='next' (SignInForm.tsx:59, SignUpForm:73, VerifyForm:69, ForgotPasswordForm:54, ResetPasswordForm:69). The authenticate action then runs safeNext(form.get('next')) again (lib/auth/actions.ts:41) before redirect(next) at :93 and :133. The second pass sees '//evil.com', hits value.startsWith('//'), and returns '/o'. Simulating the chain (repro/v/sn3.mjs) gives page '//evil.com' and action '/o' for all four attack strings. A 500k-input fuzz (repro/v/sn4.mjs) found 2141 one-pass external results and 0 two-pass external results. Other sinks cannot reach another origin. switchAccount (features/auth/actions.ts:125-132) always redirects to /sign-in?next=<encoded>. AccountChip's hidden next is an invitation path or '/o', SecurityIsland's is a constant '/account', and the forgot-password and sign-up redirects encode next into /reset-password or /verify. Only a forged direct POST to the Server Action would see single-pass output, and Next's Origin-versus-Host check on Server Actions plus the need for the victim's credentials rule that out as an ordinary-user path. The finding's own manual check (open /sign-in?next=/a/..//example.com, sign in, land on /o) already passes today.
results.correction: The stated exploit does not work. The finding's reproducer applied safeNext once, but the sign-in page and the authenticate action each apply it, so the dot-segment output '//evil.com' is re-sanitized to '/o' before redirect(). There is no reachable open redirect and no phishing consequence. What remains is a latent weakness: safeNext is not idempotent or origin-safe on its own, and tests/auth.test.mjs never exercises the dot-segment cases. Hardening safeNext (reject any result that starts with '//' or whose origin differs) plus the four test cases is cheap defense in depth, but it is a low-severity hygiene change, not a high-severity defect, and it should be dropped from the confirmed-defect list.

result.summary:
The collector gets the hard parts right. A save is one transaction. The upload body is frozen when the record is saved and re-sent with the same id after a lost response. A record is marked "Uploaded" only after the server's receipt matches it. Rejected records stay put and show a safe reason. Accounts are kept apart, and late async work is discarded after an account change. What breaks the "never lose a record" promise is how the app handles its own updates and two things it says.

1. Any SCHEMA_VERSION mismatch silently wipes every unsent observation, draft and package file before any screen appears. I reproduced it with the real code. The version was bumped twice in the week the pilot user started.
2. The Account, Sign-out and Delete-account screens tell observers the app "does not upload yet". Delete-account says it "cannot upload them first". So observers make data-losing choices at exactly the moments that matter.
3. Saved rows are re-checked against the current strict schema, one failure takes the whole read down, and the only error message is shown on a screen observers don't see. One bad row can block every map, hide all parked drafts or stop all uploads, and nothing explains why.
4. Retry delays carry over into the next foreground session. Since uploads only happen while the app is open, the observer can sit on Wi-Fi watching nothing happen for up to 5 minutes.
5. Every token refresh rebuilds the map-package machinery. That silently cancels downloads, briefly shows maps on the device as "Not downloaded", and re-verifies every package on the JS thread.
6. An idle 5-second timer bumps a counter that makes every open screen re-read the whole observations table. The Account counts and the Sign-out button flicker, and the field map is rebuilt.

The fixes are small. Most of them delete code: the "legacy" scope, the transition paths and the tables nothing reads. None needs a migration.

That is either an update that bumps it or an older build, because the check is `user_version === SCHEMA_VERSION`. git: the version went 4->5 on 2026-10-11 (a86a1ee) and 5->6 on 2026-10-13 (4eaf103). findings.current_behavior: This runs behind the Suspense splash, before any screen exists. In one transaction it drops every table, including pending, needs-attention and local-only observations, active and parked drafts, and grants. It then recreates the schema, sets package_files_need_reset and deletes Documents/hosted. There is no count, no prompt and no log. Repro: scratchpad/repro/mobile-records/reset-repro.ts runs the real initializeDatabase on node:sqlite. A v5 database with 2 unsent records and 1 draft ends with 0 observations, 0 drafts and the marker set to '1'. reset-downgrade-repro.ts (user_version 7, i.e. installing an older build) gives the same result. Welcome summaries for signed-out accounts (accounts/{id}.json) survive and keep announcing 'N records waiting' that no longer exist.
findings.consequence: A routine update destroys unsent field observations the server never received, for every account on the device. This breaks PRODUCT.md:23 'Never lose a record' and :173 'A record survives a force quit, a restart…'. The pilot is imminent and the bump cadence is days.
findings.smallest_fix: Keep the reset, as the policy allows, but refuse it when it would destroy unsent work. Inside the existing transaction, before dropping anything, count unsent observations (sync_state <> 'synced') plus active and parked drafts, tolerating missing tables. If the count is above 0, roll back and throw a typed error that the root ErrorBoundary shows as a blocking screen: 'This version cannot open N observations saved by the previous version. Do not delete the app. Install the previous version again, let them upload, then update.' Reset silently only when nothing is unsent. On reset, also delete the stale accounts/*.json summaries. No migration code.
findings.verification_scenario: Unit test: a v5 database with one pending row makes initializeDatabase reject, the row is still present and hosted/ is untouched. A database holding only synced rows resets. On a device: install build N, save a record offline, install N+1 with a bumped version. You should see the blocking screen with the record intact. Reinstall N and the record uploads.
findings.can_delete: Nothing extra is needed. No migration ladder is added.
findings.guarantee_to_keep: Pre-launch resets stay allowed whenever the device holds no unsent work. The transactional drop with rollback and the durable package-file marker stay.
findings.evidence_needed: None for the defect itself. How often pilot builds ship decides how likely it is.
findings.journey: An observer installs a new build mid-pilot with records still on the device.

findings.trigger: An observer with pending records opens Account, Sign out or Delete account, or compares the Observations tab with the Account tab.
findings.current_behavior: Account shows 'Uploaded: N' next to 'This version does not upload yet. Records stay on this device until an update of DECA Mark connects uploading.' Sign-out says 'This version does not upload yet, so they wait here either way.' The delete confirmation says 'This version cannot upload them first. They stay on this device and can never upload.' In fact the foreground uploader is live, and it stops as soon as the account signs out or is deleted. A pending record reads 'On device' on Account but 'Held' ('held for signal') on the Observations tab. Elsewhere 'Held' means local-only, waiting on the project. Uploaded records read 'Synced' on the Observations tab. findings.consequence: At the two choices where unsent research data is at stake, the app says uploading makes no difference. Deleting an account with pending records that would have uploaded within seconds makes them permanently unuploadable, so an ordinary user action loses records. Signing out on a shared tablet parks the records until that person signs in again. The mixed vocabulary breaks the DESIGN.md queue states (On device · Uploading · Uploaded · Needs attention · Held; never 'Synced').
findings.smallest_fix: Delete both 'does not upload yet' notes and the stale doc comment. Sign-out should say 'Signing out pauses their upload until this account signs in again.' On delete-account, when unsent > 0, call the existing sync.wake() and say 'Stay connected until they show Uploaded', or offer 'Upload first'. Replace records.tsx STATES with the queue.ts mapping and StateBadge, so there is one mapping. Change the heldOnly copy to 'Practice record: stays on this device'.
findings.verification_scenario: grep for 'does not upload yet' and 'cannot upload them first' returns 0 hits. With one pending record, Sign-out shows the pause sentence, and the Observations and Account tabs label that record identically ('On device'). The delete flow no longer claims uploading is impossible.
findings.can_delete: The records.tsx STATES map with its 'Held'/'Synced'/'held for signal' strings, the account 'no upload' Note and the MOB-29 comment.
findings.guarantee_to_keep: 'Uploaded' is shown only for synced rows after a receipt match. Sign-out keeps records for that account, and another account still cannot upload them.
findings.journey: An observer leaves a shared tablet or deletes their account with unsent work.

The schema files changed twice since 2026-10-08 (a86a1ee, 3612b17), and nothing checks that a tightening change bumps the version. findings.current_behavior: Active draft: readDraft returns null, hasDraft is true, unreadableDraft is set and a status message nobody renders is written. openPackage then refuses every map with 'Resume or discard the unfinished observation first.' Projects shows no unfinished card and no discard button. Parked drafts: one bad row rejects listParkedDrafts, so every parked draft vanishes from Projects and from the sign-out and delete counts. Observations: one bad row makes listObservations and pendingObservations throw. Account then says the records 'could not be counted', every 5 s drain throws so no record of that account uploads, and the raw ZodError text appears under 'Synchronisation paused'. Same invisible channel: persistDraft failures never reach Collect. Review race: dispatch(jump) during save persists with the identity still set, so a draft carrying the committed id is re-inserted after commitObservation. On restart the ghost draft is offered back and its save fails the primary key.
findings.consequence: The ordinary task stops: no map opens, or no record of the account uploads, and nothing says why. The obvious workaround, reinstalling or clearing data, destroys all unsent records. In the race case, observations collected after it lose force-quit protection while the screen says otherwise.

Render one Projects card, 'N items from an older version cannot be opened', with Discard wired to the existing discardRecovered and discardParked, or route the case into the MOB-REC-01 guard. The uploader carries on with readable rows. Drive the Collect status line from the real saveDraft result. While save() is in flight, ignore dispatch and discard using a saving ref in the session.

findings.guarantee_to_keep: Drafts never move between accounts. Recovery never substitutes another map, zone or form. Unreadable data is never removed without the observer seeing a count and choosing.
findings.evidence_needed: None for the behaviour. How likely the trigger is depends on schema-change discipline.
findings.journey: An observer updates the app with an unfinished observation, then tries to collect or upload.

findings.trigger: Flaky field signal: NetInfo reports online but requests hit the 15 s timeout, or the Render host is cold-starting. About 7 failures push a row to a 5-minute delay. The observer then opens the app on Wi-Fi, which is the only upload window because uploads happen only in the foreground.

findings.guarantee_to_keep: needs-attention stays terminal until a manual retry. Aborted requests do not count as attempts. Server Retry-After is respected.

findings.trigger: Any auth event that replaces the session object: INITIAL_SESSION at start, the hourly TOKEN_REFRESHED while in the foreground, or getSession() refreshing an expiring token. The last one happens inside the API token getter, so a download's own first request can trigger it.

The effect cleanup calls dispose(), which aborts running downloads. performDownload returns false, the provider's current() check is false, and downloads is reset to {}, so the progress simply disappears with no failure message. installed is cleared and catalog() re-reads, re-hashes and zod-validates every retained package version on the JS thread. Until it finishes, an installed site shows 'Not downloaded' and '{size} · needs a connection'. Retained versions only grow, because synced records block removal and removal never deletes files. MeProvider re-reads me.json and re-fetches /v1/me. The new projects array then makes site discovery reset its errors and re-fetch /sites for every project. At cold start this verification runs at least twice. Existing tests (provider-download.test.tsx:20-46) use one stable session object, so this path is untested.
findings.consequence: Map downloads, usually large and done on Wi-Fi before going out, are silently lost whenever a refresh lands mid-transfer. Readiness is shown falsely at every start and every refresh. Work on the JS thread grows with the number of map versions ever used, and refresh can land while collecting (cost not measured).
findings.smallest_fix: Make api, operations and the MeProvider effect depend on client, userId and `session !== null`, not on the session object. The token getter already calls getSession() for each request. Hold markAccountDeleted in a ref. Optional: list installed versions from catalog metadata at start, and verify an exact package when it is opened, not every version on every start.

findings.can_delete: The session dependencies in the two useMemos and the MeProvider effect.
findings.guarantee_to_keep: The account fence (operations recreated when userId or owner changes). Tokens are used only when session.user.id matches. A map is ready offline only after verification.
findings.evidence_needed: Hermes timing of catalog() for real hosted package sizes (archives can be up to 16 MiB, packages.py:30).
findings.journey: An observer downloads a site before fieldwork, or opens the app and checks readiness.

findings.trigger: Being signed in, in the foreground and online, with nothing queued.
findings.current_behavior: Every 5 s the drain runs a write transaction plus a pending query, then calls changed() whether or not anything changed. Repro: scratchpad/repro/mobile-records/drain-repro.ts runs the real createForegroundDrain, and 13 idle drains give 13 changed() calls. The new revision makes each focused useObservations consumer set loading=true and re-read and parse every row of the account. Account replaces its counts with 'Reading records from this device…'. Sign-out swaps its warning for a loading state and disables 'Sign out' for that moment. FieldSessionProvider consumes the sync context, so every useFieldSession consumer re-renders. findings.trigger: A development APK (local 127.0.0.1 API, possibly a different SCHEMA_VERSION) installed on the pilot Android tablet, or any preview or production build installed over another. Every one of these is com.fieldmaps.collector.dev.
findings.current_behavior: Builds replace each other in place and open the same fieldmaps-shell.db, hosted/ files and kv-store. owner_scope stores http://127.0.0.1:8000 as the API for hosted data and the hosted issuer for local-dev data, so the environment is not part of a record's identity and only the userId separates them. Staging and production point at the same backend, so there is nowhere to rehearse a schema bump before pilot devices get it. findings.evidence_needed: Whether EAS signs the development and preview APKs with the same keystore (credentials not read; EAS's per-applicationId default suggests it does).

result.assessment_markdown:
## Record classes (mobile/)

| Class | Storage | Survives kill? | Survives update with schema bump? | Survives sign-out? | Visible to other account? | User-visible wording |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Active draft | SQLite `observation_drafts`, primary key `owner_scope`, so one per account across all projects (`draft-store.ts:49-75`) | Yes. Every placement, nudge, answer, keystroke and zone change writes it (fire-and-forget, serialized FIFO). Only the last tap can be lost if killed within ms. Nothing is stored before "Place point here". | **No**: dropped silently (MOB-REC-01) | Yes, restored when the same account signs in again | No; welcome shows the count and email of the signed-out owner | "Draft kept on this device as you answer" (hard-coded even when writes fail, MOB-REC-03); card "Point placed, 3 of 8 answered. Kept on this device." An unreadable draft has **no UI** |
| Parked draft | SQLite `parked_observation_drafts` | Yes (park and restore are atomic) | **No** | Yes | No | "Keep for later" / "Keep for your coordinator"; one bad row hides all of them |
| Saved, local-only (bundled practice) | `observations` row, `local-only` | Yes (`commitObservation` inserts the record and deletes the draft in one transaction) | **No** | Yes | No | Account "Held"; Observations tab "On device only"; Saved card "Held… form not published" (wrong reason) |
| Pending | `observations` row, `pending`, frozen `uploadBody` | Yes; a lost response is re-sent with the same id and body | **No** | Yes, but uploads pause until the same account signs in | No (cannot read or upload) | Account "On device"; Observations tab "Held" / "held for signal"; Collect "N on device"; Sign-out says "does not upload yet" |
| Needs attention | `observations` row, structured `sync_error` | Yes | **No** | Yes | No | "Needs attention" plus code-specific copy (e.g. membership: "You are no longer a member…"); retry only on the Observations tab |
| Synced | `observations` row with `server_receipt`, never pruned | Yes | Local copy dropped (server keeps it) | Yes | No | Account "Uploaded" (only after `receiptMatches`); Observations tab "Synced" |
| Package files | `Documents/hosted/verified/...json`, `package_contents` (shared), `package_authorizations` (per account) | Yes; staged files are discarded at start | **No** (`hosted/` deleted) | Yes | Bytes are shared on disk but not listed without the account's own grant | "Ready offline"; shows "Not downloaded · needs a connection" while the catalog re-verifies (MOB-REC-05) |
| Caches | `me.json`, `sites-*.json`, `available_current_packages`, `last-account.json`, `accounts/{id}.json` summaries, kv-store (prefs, `fm.profile` for every user), encrypted session file + SecureStore AES key | Yes | SQLite caches dropped; files and kv survive (summaries go stale and claim N waiting) | `last-account` is removed on deliberate sign-out; the rest stay | Summaries: email and counts on welcome; everything else partitioned by user | n/a |

## Shell shown vs ready to collect (cold start)

1. **Fonts**: Splash "Opening DECA Mark".
2. **SQLiteProvider `onInit`** (behind Suspense): `user_version` check and WAL. On a mismatch, a full reset and `hosted/` deletion happen here, before any UI exists.
3. **AuthProvider `createAuthClient`**: staging and production builds read the legacy keychain entry; `last-account.json` and the deleted-account marker are read synchronously. "Opening your workspace" shows until `ready`, which is set with `session=null` and the cached account.
4. **Children mount**: MeProvider reads `me.json` synchronously; HostedSitesProvider runs `reconcileStaging` and catalog run #1 (api null); draft and parked recovery reads start. GatedStack holds a splash only when there is no local profile and `/v1/me` has not settled. **The shell is shown here.** No live session is needed; collecting works offline with a cached account.
5. **INITIAL_SESSION** arrives with a new session object. `/v1/me` is re-fetched. HostedSites `api` and `operations` are recreated, run #1 is discarded after its current package, and catalog run #2 re-reads, hashes and zod-validates every retained version on the JS thread. Until it lands, `installed=[]` and sites say "Not downloaded".
6. **TOKEN_REFRESHED** (online, expired token): run #3, plus `/v1/me` and `/sites` for every project again.
7. **Ready to collect**: the package is verified in `installed`, then Projects → Site "Set up this session" (`openPackage`, refused while an unreadable or other draft holds the slot) → Brief "Start collection" (blocked only by a resumable draft) → `/collect` (`beginVisit` takes the lease).

## Outbox vocabulary (stored state vs screens)

| Stored | Account / tab badge (`queue.ts`) | Observations tab (`records.tsx`) | Contract (`contour.json` / DESIGN) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `local-only` | Held | On device only | Held = waiting on the project |
| `pending` | On device | **Held** ("held for signal") | On device |
| (none) | Uploading (always 0) | — | Uploading = being sent now (never produced) |
| `synced` | Uploaded | **Synced** | Uploaded (never "Synced") |
| `needs-attention` | Needs attention | Needs attention | Needs attention |

"Uploaded" is never shown before a matching receipt; that part is honest.

## Account switching, privacy, membership

- **Partitioning.** Everything is keyed by `owner_scope`, and every token use checks `session.user.id === scope.userId`. The next account cannot list, open or upload the previous account's rows. Generation fences (session `current()`, sync `current()`, HostedSites epoch, `useObservations` generation) discard late async work. No listener, timer, location-watch or DB leak was found.
- **Welcome screen.** It shows other signed-out accounts' email and unsent and draft counts on a shared tablet. No record content is shown. This is acceptable for the product's "clear owner" rule; it is a disclosure of colleagues' emails only.
- **Retention.** Deleted accounts' records and all package bytes stay on the device indefinitely (`removeAccountData` has no caller; removal never deletes files). The delete-account copy says records stay, which is honest, but its "cannot upload them first" is false (MOB-REC-02).
- **At rest.** SQLite (answers, coordinates, observer initials), `me.json` (email, name, memberships) and package JSON are plaintext in `Documents/` (expo-sqlite uses `Documents/SQLite`; no backup exclusion found). They are protected by OS sandboxing and data protection, and included in device backups. The session is AES-GCM-encrypted with the key in SecureStore. This is not a finding: record it in the privacy page and IRB notes rather than encrypting the DB now.
- **Membership removed while records are queued.** There is no client-side gate. The server answers `membership_required`, the record goes to needs-attention with "You are no longer a member of this project. Contact its manager.", it stays on the device and can be retried after re-adding. Installed packages get the `no_access` problem; open, resume and download are refused. This is correct.
- **Package removal while referenced.** It is refused for any lease, draft or record, including synced records, so a map ever used can never be removed. No record risk.

## Concrete rerender chains

- **5 s tick.** `SyncProvider.setRevision` → (a) every focused `useObservations` (full-table read, `loading` flip) → `CollectScreen` → `CollectMap` new GeoJSON; (b) `FieldSessionProvider` (consumes `useSync`) → new context value → every `useFieldSession` consumer; (c) `useSiteVersions` re-queries on mounted Site and Brief screens.
- **Token refresh.** `AuthProvider` new session → `MeProvider` effect (re-fetch, new `projects`) → site discovery reset and re-fetch; HostedSites `api` → `operations` → dispose (downloads aborted), `installed=[]`, catalog re-verify; Sync effect rebuild (aborts the in-flight PUT, harmless because it is idempotent).
- **Location on.** About 1 Hz `set()` → `CollectMap` re-render (by design, limited to the map).
justified_choices: commitObservation inserts the record and deletes its draft in one SQLite transaction (observation-store.ts:56-77). A crash cannot leave both a record and its draft, or neither.

The upload body is serialized once at save (encodeUploadPayload), re-checked with uploadBodyMatches before sending, and PUT to a client-generated UUID path. A lost response is replayed unchanged, so a record uploads once.

'Uploaded' derives only from synced, and synced is written only by acknowledge after receiptSchema and receiptMatches (sync-store.ts:80-106, queue.ts:9-14). No screen claims an upload before a server receipt; 'Uploading' is never invented.

Rejections become terminal needs-attention rows with safe machine codes and local copy; server text is never echoed (upload-failure.ts:30-56, errors.ts). membership_required, conflict and idempotency_conflict all say the local record is preserved.

Aborts caused by going to the background or offline are not counted as attempts (coordinator.ts:53). A 'sign-in' result stops the coordinator, which is rebuilt when a new token arrives (provider.tsx:139 depends on sessionToken).

Account isolation by owner_scope plus a session.user.id === scope.userId check before every token use (sync, me, hosted, invitations, delete). Generation fences in every provider discard late async work after an account change.
The session is stored as AES-GCM with the key in SecureStore, with no plaintext fallback (auth-storage.ts:32-69). A cached account lets the app open and collect offline without a live session.
Sign-out keeps the account's records under its own scope and writes a summary; another account cannot upload them.

Location is foreground-only, the watcher is reference-counted by mounted maps, the fix is never stored with a record, and permission is asked only when the observer turns the dot on (use-my-location.ts).

Package installs are verified before publishing (digest, manifest, zone geometry hashes, exact forms), staged, then moved with overwrite:false. Recovery reopens the exact package, zone and form and never substitutes a newer map (ownership.ts, recovery.ts).
Package removal is refused while a lease, draft or record references the package, and the check repeats inside the transaction (package-catalog.ts:126-160).

keep_despite_complex.item: databaseWrite / databaseTransaction FIFO queue (storage/database-write.ts)
keep_despite_complex.why: expo-sqlite shares one connection. Without serialization, a draft write could join a package-removal transaction suspended at an await. It is simple and correct; only the 5 s full-table reads that pass through it should go (MOB-REC-06).

keep_despite_complex.item: Exact recovery validation (session/ownership.ts, packages/draft-recovery.ts, features/projects/recovery.ts)
keep_despite_complex.why: Research answers are only meaningful under the exact map version, zone and form they were collected with. Refusing to substitute prevents silently re-labelled data.

keep_despite_complex.item: Durable package_files_need_reset marker (initialize-collector.ts)
keep_despite_complex.why: It makes file cleanup crash-safe after a SQLite reset. Keep it alongside the MOB-REC-01 guard.

keep_despite_complex.item: In-memory package lease during a collect visit (hosted/access.ts, session-controls.ts:38-61)
keep_despite_complex.why: It stops removing or switching the map under an open visit. It is cheap and has no persistence; keep it even when deleting the dead active_sessions table.

keep_despite_complex.item: Receipt verification in bound-upload, the coordinator and acknowledge
keep_despite_complex.why: Only the acknowledge check is strictly required, because it sits at the DB boundary. The other two are redundant but cost microseconds and keep 'Uploaded' honest if code is refactored. A mismatch retrying forever (capped at 5 min) is the right failure: a record is never marked uploaded on a doubtful receipt.

keep_despite_complex.item: Generation and current() fences in AuthProvider, MeProvider, SyncProvider, HostedSitesProvider, FieldSessionProvider and useObservations
keep_despite_complex.why: They are what makes account switches and sign-outs safe mid-request. The defect in MOB-REC-05 is the dependency keys (session object identity), not the fences.

results.correction: Two separate things were bundled. (A) Review race: confirmed by the repro. A saveDraft queued behind commitObservation re-inserts a draft carrying the committed id (1 observation plus 1 ghost draft row). The next observation's saveDraft then throws DraftConflictError, a restart offers the ghost back, and saving the ghost fails 'UNIQUE constraint failed: observations.id'. Code path: ReviewStep rows have no disabled-while-saving (:171-176). onJump runs session.dispatch (CollectScreen.tsx:380-383), and dispatch persists with identity.current still set (observation-actions.ts:128-138) until reset() after the await (:191, :221). The window is the DB queue wait plus the commit transaction, tens of ms, so it is real but rare. The status line is hard-coded ('Draft kept on this device as you answer'), and session.status is rendered only by components/screen.tsx, which only the legacy records screen uses, so persist failures are invisible. (B) The headline 'unparseable row blocks every map or upload' has a hypothetical trigger. Rows are only written after the same zod schema passes, so they become unreadable only after a schema tightening without a SCHEMA_VERSION bump (a missed bump the policy would turn into a reset) or disk corruption. The history shows no such case: a86a1ee and 4eaf103 both bumped, and 3612b17 only added optional fields. The behaviour given such a row is real. Unreadable drafts are intentionally preserved (draft-store.test.ts; PACKAGE-LIFECYCLE.md:13 'blocked until explicit discard'), but the explicit-discard UI does not exist, because recovery.unreadable has no consumer. Per-row .parse in listParkedDrafts, listObservations and eligibleRows means one bad row stops the list or the batch of 25. That is poison-pill hardening against a trigger that has not occurred, not a present user-facing outage. Keep the cheap fixes: ignore dispatch and discard while save() is in flight, drive the status line from the real saveDraft result, and add the discard card (or the MOB-REC-01 guard). result.summary:
Maps, forms and package handling are mostly well built. Records freeze their package, zone and form at first placement. Recovery refuses to substitute a different package. Placement and save use the same exact closed-coverage predicate as the server. The web Data table, map and export follow the same filters, and the export says plainly that the search is not applied. None of the problems found loses a record.

The defects that matter are elsewhere. First, on Android the Collect answer panel has no keyboard avoidance (`behavior={undefined}`), even though the build is edge-to-edge and the project's own Screen.tsx comment says the window does not resize. Janet's inventory form has 8 text questions, so on the pilot Android tablet observers would type into a field the keyboard covers. Second, every token refresh rebuilds PackageOperations. That silently aborts any package download in flight, which is most likely right after resuming a stale app, and re-verifies every installed package. Third, the 5-second sync tick bumps `revision` even when nothing changed. Every focused screen then re-reads and zod-parses every record the device has ever kept. The Observations header flickers, and the Collect map re-serializes the whole package to JSON.

The other costs are real but grow with data size, and none is measured on a device. Records are never pruned and the Observations list is a plain ScrollView. The map re-stringifies the package on every render, which today is about 9 KB and costs nothing. Package install keeps about six whole-package copies, and the catalog runs again on every start. The web Data page renders each record twice (measured: 15,213 DOM nodes and 2.27 MB of HTML for 500 records). The web server re-downloads immutable archives on every plan view. On bundles, no map, editor or archive library loads where it shouldn't on either platform. The fixes are small: change a prop, change a dependency, add a guard on a callback, add a WHERE/LIMIT, pre-stringify once. None needs a new library, a worker, clustering or a different map engine.

findings.current_behavior: A new session object produces a new ApiClient, which produces a new PackageOperations.
