result.assessment_markdown:
## Data flows: maps, forms, packages and large data

Sizes: the server caps an archive at 16 MiB, its expanded contents at 80 MiB, each layer at 20,000 features and a package at 250 zones, with at most 2,000 vertices per zone and 20,000 in total. Mobile enforces the same 250 / 2,000 / 20,000 limits. The 24 MiB figure applies only to the web upload request. The real pilot data is tiny: the demo playground GeoJSON is about 9 KB.

| Flow | Data size drivers | Thread (JS/native/server) | When it runs | Retained? | Risk | Bounded change or experiment |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mobile package download (`device.ts:112-124`) | archive ≤16 MiB | native transfer; bytes then copied into JS | Site screen, Download | temp zip deleted in `finally` | Low; aborted by token refresh (MFD-2) | MFD-2 dependency fix |
| Archive SHA-256 (`device.ts:127`, expo-crypto `digest`) | archive bytes plus one copy | **native** CommonCrypto, called **synchronously** from JS | install | no | Low (native speed) | none |
| `unzipSync` → `strFromU8` → `JSON.parse` → zod (`archive.ts:24-47`) | ≤80 MiB expanded, ≤20k features per layer | JS (Hermes) | install | transient | Nil at pilot size, OOM risk at the cap (MFD-7) | heap and timing experiment with a 16 MiB archive |
| `verifyBoundZones` (canonical JSON + sha per zone, bbox) | ≤250 zones, ≤20k vertices | JS + synchronous native digest | install (×2) and every catalog load | no | Low | drop the duplicate pass |
| Install write (`installation.ts:116-159`): validate again, stringify, encode, stage, read back and compare | whole package | JS + synchronous file IO | install | file kept forever; removed versions' files never garbage-collected | Medium at the cap | compare the sha instead of the text (MFD-7) |
| `catalog()` (`operations.ts:75-104`) | sum of installed versions | JS + synchronous `textSync` | app start, **every token refresh** (MFD-2), after download or remove | every verified `StoredPackage` held in a module Map for the app's lifetime (`access.ts:7`) | Medium as packages grow | sha-only check at start; MFD-2 fix |
| Open package (`open.ts`, `build.ts:134-170`) | zones + forms | JS | open / resume | for the session | Low | — |
| CollectMap props → MapLibre (`Map.tsx:662-675`, `GeoJSONSource.tsx:235`) | ground (inside mapStyle) + paths + trees + all zones + spotlight + points | JS stringify → Fabric → native string compare | **every render**: keystroke, 5 s tick, 1 s GPS fix, pan end | strings are transient; native re-parses only on change | Low today, scales with size (MFD-6) | pre-stringify once per package |
| Zone pills and cluster bubbles (RN `Marker`s, `CollectMap.tsx:667-719`) | ≤250 zones; on-screen clusters | native view annotations + JS reconcile | every CollectMap render | while mounted | Unmeasured at 250 zones | pan FPS test with 250 zones on the Android tablet |
| Aim → placement readout (`aim-store.ts:23-35`, `useAimZone`, `CandidateEdges`) | ≤20k vertices (exact orientation) | JS | at most every 100 ms while moving, plus settle | no | Low; isolated so the map does not re-render | — |
| Prior points on the map (`mapRecords`, grid `clusterPoints`) | records at the site, unbounded | JS (O(n log n)); drawn as GPU circles | each records refresh and zoom change | no | Low–medium as history grows | `WHERE site_id` query (MFD-4) |
| `listObservations` via `useObservations` | **all** of the account's records, never deleted | SQLite native read + JS `JSON.parse` + 3-way zod union | focus, plus **every 5 s online** for each focused consumer (MFD-3) | React state, one copy per consumer | Medium (V8: 2000 records ≈ 60–100 ms) | conditional `changed()`; WHERE/LIMIT |
| Draft write (`draft-store.ts:50-75`) | one draft | serialized SQLite transaction | every answer change and keystroke | 1 row | Low; justified (survives force quit) | — |
| Observations tab (`records.tsx:83-131`) | every record | JS + native views inside a ScrollView | focus + every 5 s | all rows mounted | Medium at the 10k target (MFD-4) | unsent + newest N, or FlatList |
| Web `getSitePlan` (`workspace.ts:227-255`) | archive ≤16 MiB | **server** (Node fflate + zod + projection) | every page view with a plan (Sites ×6) | request-scoped only | Low now (MFD-8) | in-process LRU keyed by sha after the authorized read |
| Web Data page props and render | 500 per page, appended | server render + RSC payload + browser hydration | each view; "Show the next 500" | client state | Measured: 2.27 MB HTML, 15,213 nodes for 500 records (MFD-5) | render one representation |
| Web SitePlan pan/zoom (`MapFrame.tsx:415-440`) | zone vertices + markers | browser main thread; camera batched per rAF; zone path strings rebuilt each frame; background memoized (`SitePlan.tsx:369-372`) | drag, wheel, keys | no | Low; unmeasured at 250 zones / 20k vertices | performance trace while dragging with a cap-size draft |
| Web zone editor drag (`ZoneEditor.tsx:233-241`) | all zones re-projected per frame | browser; rAF-batched; problems computed only on settled zones | during a drag | no | Low | same trace |
| Web export (`ExportObservations.tsx`) | ≤10k records, server ZIP | server → browser download | on demand | no | Low; says plainly that the search is not applied | — |

**Do optional heavy modules enter initial bundles?**
- **Mobile:** no. The single Hermes bundle is 6.7 MiB. fflate is 32.7 KB and the MapLibre JS layer is 52.5 KB, both negligible. Outside this dimension, lucide-react-native is 1.54 MB (25%) because `src/ui/Icon.tsx:86` imports from the barrel.
- **Web:**
  - There is no map library; plans are hand-written SVG.
  - The zone editor loads only on its own route (1.14 MB raw app JS).
  - fflate runs on the server, apart from the browser import of `layersPlan` in the upload chunk.
  - Outside this dimension, the 391 KB raw zod chunk loads on every app route.

**Table, map, summary and export agreement (web Data):**
- The table and the map draw the same `shown` set: the loaded records narrowed by the search.
- Counts and map-version choices come from server summaries over every match.
- The export uses the server filters and says it ignores the search.
- Points recorded on another map version are dimmed, never drawn against the wrong boundaries.
- All four agree.

**Pinned versions:**
- The binding is frozen at first placement (`observation-actions.ts:86-96`).
- The draft keeps package, zone and form (`draft-persistence.ts:73-87`).
- Recovery refuses to substitute a different package (`ownership.ts`, `recovery.ts`).
- The upload body is built only from the frozen context (`wire-body.ts:31`).
- Web observation detail draws the record's own package.

No defect was found here.
justified_choices: Web plans are hand-written SVG (SitePlan/MapFrame) rather than a GL or tile map library: there is no map dependency in any bundle, 500 markers and 250 zones are within SVG's comfortable range, camera moves are batched per rAF and the background layer is memoized.
Mobile keeps MapLibre mounted across Place, Answer, Review and Saved, with an imperative camera (initialViewState plus easeTo/fitBounds), so there is no controlled-camera render loop.
Mobile draws prior observations as GPU circle layers with property-driven selection, and clusters with an O(n log n) grid only below zoom 18. That is enough without a clustering library.
The aim store is throttled to 100 ms, and the placement readout (useAimZone) and CandidateEdges are isolated so the map itself does not re-render on camera events.
Placement gating, the save re-check and zone taps all use the same exact closed-coverage predicate (zoneCovers) as the server, so the device and the server agree about edge points.

The form engine is pure and data-driven (conditions are data, there is pruning with a 'dropped' notice, and validation happens only at review). It is easy to test and matches the backend engine's semantics.
Drafts are written on every keystroke through serialized SQLite transactions, deliberately without debouncing so a force quit loses nothing; the cost is one small row.

Records and drafts freeze the package, zone and form binding at first placement, and recovery refuses substitution. The web observation detail and the Data map honour the version each record was collected on.
Web Data keeps the table, map, counts and export consistent, and states honestly what each one covers (the subset note, the search-not-applied note).
SHA-256 runs through expo-crypto's native digest rather than a JS implementation.
Web keeps a small per-account LRU of site plans (packagePlans, 8 entries) so switching versions on the Data map does not re-fetch.
Zone editor drags are batched per rAF, and problems are computed on settled zones, not on every frame.

keep_despite_complex.item: Exact orientation predicate with a BigInt fallback (mobile/src/maps/zone-boundaries.ts:52-133)
keep_despite_complex.why: Without it, a point exactly on an edge could be accepted on the device and rejected by the server as point_outside_zone, and the record would land in needs-attention. It only falls back to BigInt for nearly collinear points, so it is cheap.

keep_despite_complex.item: Per-zone geometry_sha256 plus manifest/layer identity checks at install (verify-bound.ts:9-97)
keep_despite_complex.why: They guarantee the polygon used to gate placement is exactly the server's zone snapshot that the record binds to. Keep the check once at install; only the duplicate pass is waste.

results.correction: The core claim holds: KAV is a no-op on Android and nothing else lifts the panel. Platform behaviour is not device-verified. adjustResize not resizing under decorFitsSystemWindows(false) is documented Android behaviour and the project's own comment in Screen.tsx says so. Three corrections. (1) Severity high is too high: the pilot is a tablet, where the field is probably visible and the Back/Continue row is hidden, with a workaround of dismissing the keyboard. Phones in portrait are worse, because the 46% map stack puts the panel almost entirely under the keyboard, so medium is honest. (2) Layout is by orientation, not device class: layout.wide is !portrait (use-layout.ts:36), so phones in landscape also get the side-by-side panel, and portrait tablets get the 46% stack. (3) Single-line TextInputs have returnKeyType=next with onSubmitEditing=onAdvance (QuestionStep.tsx:~211-218), which partly mitigates single-line text and number questions. It does not cover the multi-line Textareas, which are most of the text questions. The smallest fix of behavior="padding" on both platforms is right.

results.checked: Traced end to end. auth/provider.tsx:160-195 calls setState with the new session object on every auth event, including TOKEN_REFRESHED. session-retention.ts:14-17 and sessionIdentity return the session itself. In provider.tsx, `api` depends on [client, session, userId] (:50-59) and only `session` changes by identity (userId, owner and issuer are strings). `operations` depends on [api, database, issuer, owner] (:61-77) and runs `++generation.current` inside the memo, so the OLD operations' runtime.current() goes false as soon as the new memo is computed. The effect cleanup then calls dispose(), which aborts the controllers (operations.ts:51-55). performDownload returns false (:196-198, :193), and installVerifiedPackage throws when current() is false, which is caught. The provider then returns silently at provider.tsx:129 with no failure recorded. The new effect runs setDownloads({}) and setInstalled([]) (:97-98) and reload(), which calls catalog(). catalog() re-reads, re-hashes, JSON.parses, zod-parses and validateStored-checks every installed version (operations.ts:75-104, installation.ts:71-104). Downloads are user-initiated only (HostedPackageIsland.tsx:89, data-source.tsx:103) with no auto-retry. No test covers a session identity change: provider-download.test.tsx mocks a static session. auth-js 2.117.3: constants.js:6,9,13 (30 s tick, 3 ticks, 90 s margin); GoTrueClient.js:4287 notifies TOKEN_REFRESHED with a fresh data.session; :4484-4490 runs an immediate tick; supabase/config.toml:164 jwt_expiry=3600.
results.correction: The claim is confirmed. Corrections: (1) The silent return is at provider.tsx:129, inside download() at :105-146, not :125-129. (2) "Near-certain when Download is tapped right after resuming" is overstated. The resume tick fires at about t=0, so the refresh usually finishes before the observer navigates to Download. A better trigger is GoTrueClient.js:4126-4128, where getSession() itself refreshes when the token is within 90 s of expiry or stale. The download's own first request (the token getter at provider.tsx:53-55) can therefore cause the TOKEN_REFRESHED that aborts it. That fits the first download after a long background period or after a failed resume refresh. (3) The odds are low for seconds-long pilot downloads of tiny (~9 KB) packages, so medium is the upper end. The hourly catalog re-verify and the briefly empty `installed` list are real, but their cost scales with installed package bytes. The one-line fix is right, but compute `const signedIn = session !== null` first so the hook-deps lint stays clean.

The drain is activateHeldObservations (sync-store.ts:43-78, a databaseTransaction BEGIN IMMEDIATE plus SELECT on every tick, even with no local-only rows) followed by the coordinator, which returns void and exits early when nothing is pending. use-observations.ts: refresh always calls setLoading(true) (:20), and useFocusEffect depends on [refresh, revision] (:46). results.correction: Confirmed. Refinements. (1) Real changes still fire changed(): wake() at provider.tsx:51-54 and retryNow at :108-115 call it directly. (2) The fix is not delete-only: createSyncCoordinator and activateHeldObservations return void, so both must report whether they acknowledged, deferred or activated anything before changed() can be made conditional. (3) site-versions.ts:37,78 also consumes sync.revision and runs zoneReferences per installed entry every tick on site screens. That is another beneficiary of the fix and another cost the finding omits. (4) 'Any screen' is really any screen whose useFocusEffect consumer is focused: the tabs layout, Collect and the Observations screen. (5) Cost at pilot scale (dozens of records) is negligible. The 5 s 'Reading local records…' flicker and the 5 s BEGIN IMMEDIATE write transaction are certain. Hermes cost is unmeasured, so medium holds only at hundreds of records or more.

results.checked: records.tsx:83-131 mounts every record (about 7-8 host views each) inside PageScreen, which is a ScrollView (components/screen.tsx:35-50). listObservations (observation-store.ts:79-101) filters only by owner_scope, with no LIMIT. mapRecords (records.ts:20-37) filters the whole account array in JS. No DELETE FROM observations exists in mobile src except account-removal.ts:45 (account deletion). results.correction: The core claim holds (unbounded read, parse and mount) and the category is honest, but there are three corrections. (1) The Collect fix `WHERE site_id` does not work: the observations table has no site_id column (database-migrations.ts:9-17 has id, created_at, payload, owner_scope, sync_state, sync_error, server_receipt, attempts, next_attempt_at and package_key), and package_key is per package version. It needs json_extract(payload,'$.siteId') or a new column with a SCHEMA_VERSION bump, and a bump resets the schema and wipes unsent records. The Observations-tab fix (non-synced rows in full, newest N synced, plus a COUNT) works with the existing sync_state column and indexes. (2) docs/Production-Architecture-Recommendation.md:145-151 calls 10,000 observations and a 500 MB package 'proposed engineering acceptance targets, not measured capacity' to be replaced with pilot measurements, so it is not a documented requirement. (3) Severity medium is unearned for an unmeasured effect: pilot volumes are likely tens to hundreds of records. Low until Hermes timings on the pilot tablet show otherwise.

result.summary: The pattern across this codebase is not too much abstraction. The policy is applied in the wrong place. The owner's "resets are fine" rule protects development databases, but the collector applies it to the observer's phone. initializeDatabase drops every SQLite table, unsent records and drafts included, whenever SCHEMA_VERSION changes. That happened twice in three days (5 on 10-11, 6 on 10-13), and nothing is counted or warned about first. The same missing non-destructive path is why a frozen "legacy" owner_scope stays the account key: three of its four fields are constants (127.0.0.1:8000, the hosted issuer and a fixed project), and issuer checks compare one constant with another. Changing the key today would orphan every pending row. Next by impact is the release Observations tab. It is still the pre-Contour (Nocturne) records screen, with its own status words: pending shows as "Held" and synced as "Synced", against PRODUCT.md's vocabulary. That screen also drags about 1 MB of Inter fonts in front of the first frame. The duplicated rules are mostly deliberate and fairly cheap: a byte-copied form engine, per-platform primitives over one token contract, and error tables checked against the generated ErrorCode type. But the guards that make the copies safe do not run: forms:parity, the web unit tests (393) and tokens:check are absent from CI, while the docs present them as checks. Web also keeps a fourth, unguarded form model (answers.ts) that exists mainly for the legacy `fields` format, which the backend dropped in 577959a. Leftovers from the rename (11 redirects, old service-worker cache names, the fieldmaps:// scheme, the SecureStore migration) and several write-only mobile tables can go without losing any guarantee. The security boundaries hold up. In particular, the reported safeNext open redirect cannot be reached end to end, because the sign-in action applies safeNext again and refuses "//host". Change cost is moderate. The worst traps are (1) a strict filter schema in Data's server action that TypeScript does not tie to ObservationFilters, (2) question-kind renderers written as if-chains that compile when a kind is missing, and (3) LAYER_NAMES declared in five places.

findings.trigger: Any build that changes SCHEMA_VERSION (git history: 5 in a86a1ee on 2026-10-11, 6 in 4eaf103 on 2026-10-13) is installed over a build whose device holds local-only/pending records, an active draft or parked drafts. Removing legacyScope, as the no-legacy policy suggests, changes owner_scope and orphans the same rows.
findings.current_behavior: On first open after the update, PRAGMA user_version != 6, so initializeDatabase drops observations, observation_drafts, parked_observation_drafts and the rest inside one transaction, recreates empty tables and flags package files for deletion. Nothing counts unsent rows first and nothing tells the observer. Separately, every account's storage key is JSON ["http://127.0.0.1:8000", <hosted issuer>, userId, <fixed project>], whatever the real connection. The issuer checks in bound-upload.ts:20 and receipt.ts:24 compare that constant with itself, and package identities and device paths (installation.ts:22-24,123, device.ts:50-52) carry the same constant issuer.
findings.consequence: Ordinary updates silently destroy records that were never uploaded. That directly breaks PRODUCT.md's promise that observers never lose a record, and it is reachable during the Janet's Play Study pilot. Because no non-destructive path exists, the legacy key can never be deleted, so a 4-field identity with 3 dead fields (and the checks built on it) is carried in sync, package catalog and file layout.
findings.smallest_fix: Do not migrate; preserve and refuse to hide. In initializeDatabase, when user_version is neither 0 nor SCHEMA_VERSION: (1) count observations WHERE sync_state != 'synced' plus rows in both draft tables. (2) If the count is above zero, run `VACUUM INTO '<documents>/set-aside/v<old>-<timestamp>.db'` before the DROP; VACUUM INTO must run outside the transaction. (3) Write the count into local_metadata, and show one plain notice on Collect and Observations: 'N records from the previous app version were kept on this phone but not uploaded. Tell your study lead.' Freeze SCHEMA_VERSION for the pilot. Once the guard exists, replace legacyScope with a userId-only key in the next schema bump, then delete data/legacy/scope.ts, the constant-issuer checks and receipt.ts:4's caveat. Keep the DB name and bundle ids (renaming either creates an empty store).
findings.can_delete: After the guard: data/legacy/scope.ts, the apiUrl/issuer/projectId fields of SyncScope used only as key material, and the constant-versus-constant issuer comparisons
findings.guarantee_to_keep: A record or draft written to SQLite is never destroyed without the observer being told. Account isolation by userId. Verified receipt matching (observation, user, project, package and zone ids).
findings.verification_scenario: Unit: seed a v5 database with 2 pending observations and 1 draft, run initializeDatabase at v6, and assert the set-aside file exists with 3 rows and local_metadata holds the count. Device: install the current build, save 2 records in airplane mode, install a build with SCHEMA_VERSION 7, and confirm the notice shows 2 and the file under Documents/set-aside opens in sqlite3 with both rows.

## (b) Change-cost walkthroughs: files that must change today

**1. Add a new question type (for example `date`).**
- Backend: form_definition.py:62 (Literal), form_engine.py:104-121 (assert_never forces it), forms.py:52-71, form_references.py:43-136 (condition rules), observation_export_columns.py:110 and observation_export_plan.py:47 (values).
- Contracts: run `pnpm contracts:generate` (openapi.json, form-definition.schema.json:107-114 and both schema.d.ts, guarded by the CI diff), plus contracts/forms cases.
- Mobile: forms/definition.ts:76 (zod enum), engine.ts:71-75 and 128, session.ts:108 (write conversion), features/collect/QuestionStep.tsx:107-215 (input).
- Web: re-copy lib/forms/{definition,engine}.ts; features/forms/raw.ts:78-91 (starter), QuestionSettings.tsx:29-48, model.ts:182 (FORMAT_LABEL is a Record, so tsc forces it), CollectorPreview.tsx:168-496, lib/observations/answers.ts:116 (KINDS; an unknown kind falls back to 'text').

That is about 16 files plus tests. The unnecessary cost: QuestionStep and CollectorPreview are if-chains, so forgetting them compiles and renders a question with no input; answers.ts is a fourth copy of the rules; and parity is not in CI. Lowering it: switch-with-assert_never in the two renderers, plus S4 and S3. A mobile build without the new kind refuses the package rather than misrendering it (packages/open.ts:20-23), which is correct.

**2. Add a filter to Data, Reports, map and export.**
- Backend: domain/observation_filters.py, routers/observation_analysis.py, repositories/observation_analysis.py, observation_analysis_schemas.py and the export, then contracts:generate.
- Web, shared mapping: lib/api/observations.ts:82-101 (ObservationFilters and filterQuery, the single mapping used by list, summary and export; good).
- Web, Data: features/data/view.ts (DataView :29-46, parseView :83-101, viewQuery :105-117, hasFilters :120, viewFilters :136-150, doc table :13-21), data/actions.ts:26-36 (strict zod; runtime-only trap, S7), FilterBar.tsx, DataScreen.tsx:417 (filter words).
- Web, Reports: reports/page.tsx:24-69 and ReportsScreen.tsx:81-86 (a separate parser and URL builder).

The map and export inherit the filter for free. That is about 10 web files. Lowering it: a `satisfies` tie on filtersSchema, and Reports reusing parseView/viewFilters (deletes about 30 lines).

**3. Add a typed map layer to packages.**
- Backend: domain/packages.py:32-33 and archive building, then contracts:generate (openapi.json:2704-2716 already enumerates layer names).
- Web: lib/packages.ts:14-47,118-119 (names, required, order, labels, geometry kinds, name guess), lib/sites/archive.ts:69-78,240-293 (private duplicate list, schema, projection), features/packages/upload-preview.ts:14 (inline list), lib/plan.ts and components/map/SitePlan.tsx / MapFrame.tsx (drawing), contracts/map-palettes.json.
- Mobile: packages/hosted/archive.ts:12, schemas.ts:30-36, build.ts:79-103 (overlay and paint), maps/palette.ts.

That is about 11 files; 2 of the 5 name lists are pointless duplicates. Lowering it: derive from the generated type (S8). Install verification (verify-bound.ts, installation.ts) only covers zones, so it needs no change unless the new layer becomes required.

**4. Change a shared control (Button size or variant) in both apps.** web/src/components/contour/Button.tsx:9-77 (SIZE, VARIANT and DISABLED maps) and mobile/src/ui/Button.tsx:7-90 (lookOf switch, size table). A colour change is one edit to contracts/contour.json followed by `pnpm tokens` (scripts/contour-tokens.mjs generates web/src/styles/contour.css, and mobile reads ui/tokens.ts). Two files for a variant change is the right cost: web sizes are 46/36/56 px, mobile 56/60/44 px, and web has ghost where mobile has link. A shared cross-platform component would add a framework for no gain. The only gap is that tokens:check is not in CI (S3).

## Claims checked and rejected
- **The safeNext open redirect (web-data-identity F3) cannot be reached.** The page's safeNext turns "/a/..//evil" into "//evil" for the hidden input. But lib/auth/actions.ts:41 (authenticate) and features/auth/actions.ts:125 (switchAccount) call safeNext(form.get("next")) again, and "//evil" fails the startsWith("//") check, so the result is "/o". Reproduced in scratchpad/repro/simp/safenext.mjs. No client code calls router.push(next). What remains: safeNext is not idempotent, so a future direct redirect of the page-level value would open the hole. A two-line origin check fixes that.
- **Zod in web client bundles.** The zod/openapi-fetch chunk (391 KB raw, 90.7 KB gzip, static-bundle.json) loads on every /o route (cold.json). One path is LoadFailure, which imports isNoAccess from lib/workspace/result.ts, which imports zod through lib/api/errors.ts. But 13 other client modules legitimately pull zod-bearing libraries, so moving isNoAccess saves bytes only on routes without them. The benefit is unmeasured; this is not reported as a finding.
- **Sampled comments that claim guarantees.** "One transaction: a record can never be stored while its draft survives" (session/observation-actions.ts:189) holds: observation-store.ts:63-77 inserts the record and deletes the draft in one databaseTransaction. The false guarantee lives in the docs instead: PRODUCT.md promises no record loss (S1), and AGENTS.md:20 describes tokens:check as enforcing (S3).
justified_choices: Byte-copied form engine (mobile is the source, web the copy) checked by a parity script: each app owns its own lockfile (pnpm-workspace.yaml packages: []), so a copy is the cheapest way to share. It just needs to run in CI.
The backend's own form engine (fieldmaps_api/domain/form_engine.py): the server has to validate uploads itself, so this is not duplication to remove.

Per-platform Contour primitives over one token contract (contracts/contour.json -> scripts/contour-tokens.mjs -> web contour.css and mobile ui/tokens.ts): sizes and variants differ for good reasons (web md 46 px vs mobile md 56 px plus a collector size).

Per-platform error copy tables declared `satisfies Readonly<Record<ErrorCode,string>>` (web/src/lib/api/errors.ts:40, mobile/src/data/api/errors.ts:36): exhaustive at compile time, with wording that may differ by platform.
A single filter-to-API mapping (web/src/lib/api/observations.ts:93-101 filterQuery) shared by list, summary and the browser export, so the map, counts and export cover the same matches.
The CI contracts job regenerates openapi.json and both schema.d.ts and fails on any diff (.github/workflows/ci.yml:9-25).

Web dependencies are lean (12): radix-ui for 9 accessible primitives (Dialog, Checkbox, DropdownMenu, Popover, RadioGroup, Switch, Toast, ToggleGroup, Tooltip), cmdk for the command palette only, fflate for archive reading only, openapi-fetch in 2 modules, server-only on 7 server modules.
Mobile uses ky with generated types for the API and supabase-js only for auth, one stack per concern, not two clients for the same API.

Dev and preview surfaces are gated server-side or at the route (web notFound() unless NODE_ENV is development or NEXT_PUBLIC_PREVIEW_TOOLS; mobile app/(dev)/_layout.tsx:12 Redirect unless PREVIEW_ALLOWED).
dangerouslySetInnerHTML is used only for the constant THEME_SCRIPT (app/layout.tsx:54, global-error.tsx:22).

keep_despite_complex.item: mobile/src/platform/auth-storage.ts:25-68: AES-GCM session file with its key in SecureStore, and no plaintext fallback
keep_despite_complex.why: Keeps the refresh token encrypted at rest without hitting SecureStore's size limits, and treats corrupt storage as signed out instead of falling back to plaintext. Only the legacy migration function at :81-95 should go.

keep_despite_complex.item: mobile/src/storage/observation-store.ts:63-77 commitObservation (insert the record and delete its draft in one transaction) and storage/database-write.ts serialization
keep_despite_complex.why: These enforce the durable-record guarantee and stop a draft being offered again under an id already stored.

keep_despite_complex.item: Receipt and body matching: mobile/src/sync/receipt.ts:22-33 (ids) and sync/wire-body.ts uploadBodyMatches
keep_despite_complex.why: A record is marked synced only when the server's receipt matches its observation, user, project, package and zone. Only the issuer comparison is ceremonial (S1).

keep_despite_complex.item: Verified package installation: mobile/src/packages/hosted/archive.ts schema checks, verify-bound.ts zone and digest checks, installation.ts identity checks
keep_despite_complex.why: This is what stops a tampered or mismatched package from being used for collection. Do not simplify it away along with the duplicated layer constants.

keep_despite_complex.item: web/src/lib/pwa/service-worker.js:26-35 safeResponse and the RSC/Authorization bypass at :80
keep_despite_complex.why: It caches only public, non-private, non-RSC responses from the same origin, so private workspace data never lands in Cache Storage. Delete only the legacy cache names.

keep_despite_complex.item: web/src/proxy.ts:44-48 Cache-Control: private, no-store and Referrer-Policy: no-referrer on every non-public response
keep_despite_complex.why: Keeps authenticated pages out of shared caches and keeps invitation and secret URLs out of Referer headers.

keep_despite_complex.item: web/src/features/data/actions.ts filtersSchema and the access re-check in loadObservationsAction
keep_despite_complex.why: Server Actions are public endpoints, so re-validating filters and re-resolving project access is required. Tie its type to ObservationFilters (S7); do not remove it.

keep_despite_complex.item: safeNext applied on both the page and the action (web/src/lib/auth/navigation.ts:4-17, lib/auth/actions.ts:41)
keep_despite_complex.why: Applying it a second time is what currently blocks the dot-segment redirect. Make it idempotent, but keep both calls.

keep_despite_complex.item: Invitation secrets kept in the URL hash and in tab-scoped sessionStorage (web/src/features/auth/invitation.ts:10-15,94-97), and mobile +native-intent.tsx:12-20 storing only the join code
keep_despite_complex.why: The secret never reaches a server log, and joining always needs an explicit confirmation press (join-project.tsx and invitation/[code].tsx).

keep_despite_complex.item: mobile/src/storage/database-migrations.ts package_files_need_reset marker and the initialize-collector.ts retry
keep_despite_complex.why: It makes filesystem cleanup crash-safe. Keep it when adding S1's set-aside step.

keep_despite_complex.item: web/src/lib/supabase/server.ts:17-24 narrow catch of Next's 'Cookies can only be modified' error
keep_despite_complex.why: It swallows only the documented case where a Server Component cannot set cookies (the text was confirmed in next 16.2.7 request-cookies.js), not all errors.

not_covered: Nothing was run on a device or simulator (read-only audit): S1's wipe was traced in code and git history only, and S9's startup benefit is unmeasured.
The web rendering/caching performance (server fan-out, archive re-download per plan view) and the mobile revision/refresh churn were left to the other dimension audits.
Backend internals beyond the files needed for the change-cost walkthroughs and the 577959a legacy removal.
Hosted database contents: whether fields-only form_versions rows exist was not queried (the evidence_needed for S4).
The email templates half of tokens:check and the QGIS plugin code.
Accessibility and visual design of the screens named here, beyond the status vocabulary.

results.checked: Read database-migrations.ts, initialize-collector.ts, app/_layout.tsx:105-107, legacy/scope.ts, session-retention.ts, contracts.ts, receipt.ts, bound-upload.ts, hosted/provider.tsx:33, installation.ts, device.ts and sync-store.ts. All cited line refs are accurate. Git history confirmed: schema 5 in a86a1ee (2026-10-11), schema 6 in 4eaf103 (2026-10-13). Mechanism confirmed. When user_version differs from 6, initializeDatabase (lines 55-89) drops every table and view in sqlite_master and recreates empty tables inside one transaction. It never counts unsent rows or drafts, no UI notice exists, and initialize-collector.ts then clears package files. The legacy key is also confirmed. accountWorkspace always builds [http://127.0.0.1:8000, hosted lezmq issuer, userId, fixed project] and ignores the real connection (config/staging and production use the onrender API; development uses a local Supabase). bound-upload.ts:20 and receipt.ts:24 compare record.binding.issuer with scope.issuer, and both come from the same constant. Refuting context: (1) The wipe is documented, deliberate policy. docs/plan/README.md:10-14 (Pre-launch compatibility policy, 2026-10-11) says there are no preservation obligations and that old-schema upgrade paths must not be added to retain experimental data. mobile/ZONE-BOUNDARIES.md:18 (MOB-28) says to reset on a version mismatch. mobile/README.md:314 and MOB-33-HANDOFF.md:128 say schema 6 deliberately resets. docs/plan/zone-boundaries/README.md:35 says a deliberate schema reset is the only thing that clears local data. (2) docs/plan/current-state.md says the work is not yet pilot-ready, the demo data is synthetic, and the schema has stayed at 6 on purpose (the mob29 review confirms no reset), so nothing is lost today. (3) Counterweight: the newest docs in HEAD, docs/reviews/fields-only-transition-2026-10-17/README.md:15 and docs/reviews/published-form-compatibility-2026-10-17/inventory.md, say an explicit instruction to preserve unknown existing data takes precedence over the earlier reset policy. They also say custody must be defined before device upgrades or resets, because a storage reset does not preserve queued work. So the hazard is recognised, but no guard has been decided. (4) The legacy-key half: mobile/README.md:339 and PLAN.md:90 freeze the key until MOB-11, and MOB-11 was reconciled to no migration. Under the stated reset policy the key can be removed with a schema bump and reset.
results.correction: Keep the mechanism as a latent data-loss hazard, not a CONFIRMED DEFECT: severity medium, not critical. Nothing is lost today because no bump is pending; the loss needs a future SCHEMA_VERSION change over a device with unsent records. Reset-on-mismatch is documented MOB-28 behaviour. The claim 'ordinary updates silently destroy records' is too broad; only schema-bumping builds do. The claim that the legacy key 'can never be deleted' or 'cannot be removed safely' is wrong under the documented policy, where bump plus reset is the sanctioned way to remove it. The 4-field key with 3 dead fields and the constant-versus-constant issuer checks are real complexity, but the finding's 'guard first, then delete' ordering is a data-preservation ask the Oct 11 policy does not require. The cheap, real mitigation is a release rule: freeze SCHEMA_VERSION once real observers hold unsent records, and when the owner confirms preserve-over-reset, add the count-and-set-aside guard. Minor: initializeDatabase spans lines 55-89, not 55-88.

result.summary:
The web manager workspace is mostly honest and careful. Counts say when they are capped ("Showing 1–500 of 520 · counted at 12:14"), dates carry the project time zone, unbuilt features get a NotAvailable note instead of a fake button, and the export dialog repeats its scope, says the search is not applied and refuses more than 10,000 records. For one site, the site page answers "what does an observer download right now?" correctly: package version, form version and inventory form.

The problems sit where the manager has to connect separate objects: a QGIS export, a form version, a map package and an observer.

1. **Misleading upload error.** When the server blocks a map upload during package preparation, the reason is discarded. The manager is told a zone's rings are malformed. This happens with any QGIS project that has an online basemap, and the lab's real Ithaca project does.
2. **No way to tell which form observers use.** The Forms list pairs the newest published version with sites that actually use an older one. Overview then says "Nothing needs attention." Publishing a form never reaches observers until the whole QGIS export is uploaded again. That re-upload asks the manager to confirm each zone one at a time, and it silently replaces any boundaries edited on the web.
3. **Data map out of reach on iPad.** Below 1280 px (every iPad and many laptops) the site plan is drawn after up to 500 table rows. This contradicts DESIGN.md's 768 px rule.
4. **Invitations.** The join code and link are shown once, and pressing Esc or tapping the dim background closes that dialog and loses them. Invitation emails that fail are never reported.
5. **Smaller defects.**
   - The observer filter is case-sensitive, so typing lowercase initials says nothing matches.
   - Returning from an observation via the "Data" breadcrumb drops the filters.
   - In an empty project, the one highlighted button points at an empty Data page.

The web code is identical between the audited commit 9928f53 and the current HEAD b93a2b2. Nothing was rendered at tablet widths, so the iPad layout and upload-feedback claims come from reading the code and CSS.

findings.trigger: There are three triggers. (1) On the 'Invitation ready' dialog, the manager presses Esc or taps the dim area around the dialog before copying; on an iPad this is an easy accidental tap. (2) An addressed invitation whose Brevo delivery later fails; hosted delivery is unverified. (3) The manager leaves email empty, expecting a join code for the whole team as the hint says, and keeps the default of 1 use.
findings.current_behavior: (1) The dialog closes and the code and link are gone for good. The invitation stays valid and appears as one more indistinguishable 'Join code' row. (2) The manager only ever sees 'queued'. The outbox's later failed status reaches no screen. (3) The second observer gets 'no longer works… used up'.
findings.consequence: Observers cannot join and the manager does not know why. Recovery is revoke and recreate, but with several identical 'Join code' rows the manager cannot tell which to revoke, so a stray valid code stays live until it expires.
findings.smallest_fix: Once an invitation is created, keep the dialog open on Esc and outside taps (preventDefault in onEscapeKeyDown and onInteractOutside), so only Done closes it, or ask 'Close without copying?'. Show the created time on Join code rows. ## Scope and evidence

## Novice vs experienced (heuristic)
- **Novice manager:**
  - The setup order loops: package → form → package.
  - Two QGIS project inputs with different meanings, and red "Fails" badges before anything is chosen.
  - Terms like "Inventory form" and "Which zone is each zone in the file?".
  - The invite hint suggests a multi-use code but the default is 1.
  - The misleading upload error (UXW-1) is the worst trap.
- **Experienced manager:**
  - Repeated work on every form revision: re-upload and re-confirm every zone (UXW-4).
  - Lost filters on return from a record (UXW-7).
  - Exact-case observer filter (UXW-6).
  - On iPad, no usable map (UXW-3).
- **Both:**
  - Inconsistent answers to "which form are observers on?" (UXW-2).

## Current vs proposed interactions

**1. Getting a corrected form to observers**
- Current: Forms → editor → Save → Publish → tick the box → Publish play-v2 → toast → versions list → (manager must remember) Sites → Fall Creek → Upload a new version → choose .qgz + sources → Read project → check Form version = play-v2 → for each of N zones pick "Same zone as …" → Upload package → (if the zones were edited on the web, the boundaries silently revert). Meanwhile the Forms list shows "Published play-v2 · Used by Fall Creek" and Overview shows "Nothing needs attention".
- Proposed: Forms → editor → Save → Publish → tick the box → Publish play-v2. The publish result lists "Fall Creek uses play-v1 — [Use play-v2 on Fall Creek's map]", which publishes map vN+1 from the current archive with play-v2. Until that is done, Overview shows a waiting item "play-v2 is published; no site's map names it", and the Forms list reads "Fall Creek · play-v1".

**2. Uploading a real QGIS project that has a basemap**
- Current: choose .qgz + gpkg → Read project ("N layers read… Imagery and QGIS styling are not imported.") → Upload package → "Not uploaded. A zone's shape could not be read. Check that each of its rings is closed…". The manager edits zones in QGIS, re-exports and gets the same error.
- Proposed: Read project lists "Basemap 'OpenStreetMap' (tile service) will block the package: remove it from the project, or upload without the project file". If the manager uploads anyway: "Not uploaded. Imagery licence: OpenStreetMap (tile.openstreetmap.org) is fetched from a tile service on demand… Remove the layer or supply institution-owned imagery."

**3. Reviewing a filtered set on an iPad**
- Current: Data → set Site, Round and Observer (initials must be uppercase) → table of up to 500 rows, with the plan after the last row → tap a row (nothing visible changes) → open record → "Data" breadcrumb → filters gone.
- Proposed: Data → set filters (initials are uppercased) → the plan sits above the table (compact), or beside it at xl as a sticky panel → tapping a row highlights the point in view → open record → "Data" breadcrumb returns to the same filtered URL.

## The "one magenta action per screen" rule
- Helps on: Site (Upload a new version), Upload (Upload package), Publish (Publish vN), Team (Invite), Data (Export) and Reports (Print).
- Obstructs on Overview for an empty project (UXW-8): the static primary points away from setup.
- No screen shows two primaries in code; the honesty e2e scans for this (`web/e2e/support/scan.ts`).

## Voice and copy
- No "successfully", "Oops", Synced/Pending/Failed labels or bare OK/Submit were found in `web/src`.
- Implementation vocabulary leaks in a few places: "Revision" on the observation detail, and the History "Forms" column shows two unlabelled codes that wrap mid-code (packages-upload.png).
- The doc conflict PRODUCT.md:55 J1 (packages before forms) contradicts the code's prerequisite.
justified_choices: Honest delivery copy at every point a manager might assume observers already have something: the form publish screen says 'Observers collect with X only through a map package that names it' and requires a checkbox (`forms/model.ts:285-296`). The site page says 'Observers get this version the next time they make the site ready offline' (`SiteScreen.tsx:258-261`). Device readiness is a NotAvailable note instead of a guess.

Capped data is stated in place, not hidden: 'Showing 1–500 of N matching observations · counted at HH:MM', 'Show the next 500', 'The map shows the 500 loaded of N', and the Reports and Overview sampled notes (`view.ts:368-384`, `map.ts:160-173`, `ReportsScreen.tsx:313-319`). With paging plus server totals, virtualization is unnecessary at pilot scale.
The Data view keeps all its state in the URL (`view.ts` parseView/viewQuery) with 'Copy link to this view', so Back, sharing and refresh work without extra client state.

The export dialog repeats the scope in words, says the search is not applied, states the 10,000 cap and says device-held records are excluded (`ExportObservations.tsx:105-147`). This matches the PRODUCT.md honesty rules exactly.
Every date surface names the project time zone (`FilterBar.tsx:156`, `FieldReturnIsland.tsx:94-96`, `ReportsScreen.tsx:256-257,365`), and the detail page shows both observed and uploaded times.
Each section fails on its own with a LoadFailure instead of showing zero (Overview `page.tsx:114-135`), and AttentionIsland refuses to claim 'nothing needs attention' when a check could not run.

Destructive actions confirm in a dialog with a danger-solid button (remove member, revoke, retire with the sites using it, discard draft). Retiring is refused while a current package binds the version.
The observation detail is read against the form version and map version it was collected with ('v2 is current' is added), so evidence stays traceable, as PRODUCT.md principle 5 requires.

results.checked: Confirmed the structural claims. PublishScreen.tsx:~175-194 and forms/model.ts:285-296 (deliveryOf) say observers get a new version only through a new map package and link to Sites. The backend DraftPublish carries only request_id and expected_current_package_id (backend/src/fieldmaps_api/zone_draft_schemas.py:55-58). Zone publish builds PublishJob(forms=current.forms) from the retained archive (services/zone_publication.py ~139-152), and PublishReview.tsx:620-633 shows the forms read-only. The only form-binding route is POST /v1/projects/{p}/packages (routers/sites.py:86). UploadStep requires ground and zones (reason text :389-407). The form-version Select is at UploadStep.tsx:486-496. ZoneMapping.tsx:47-51,55-128 has one Select per zone, the copy 'A matching code or name does not make it the same zone.' and no bulk action. identity.ts:78-96 makes a code or name match only a suggestion (choice 'undecided'). zones/model.ts:21-26 shows zone editing is available whenever zone_editing_available. UploadStep.tsx:808-849 (ServerResult) after upload shows only version, zone count and bytes. The upload UI has no geometry-change note; the only note is 'Removed from the next version' (ZoneMapping.tsx:130-135).
results.correction: Two factual corrections and one reframing. (1) 'Nothing compares the file's zone geometry with the current version' is inaccurate. The server does compute it: validate_zone_import (queries/zones.py:74 IMPORT_VALIDATE) calls fieldmaps_private.zone_validation (supabase/migrations/20261012120000_current_baseline.sql ~1756-1830), which sets a per-zone change of added/removed/geometry_changed/label_changed/unchanged (ZoneValidationSummary.change, zone_response_schemas.py:64). import_package only calls require_ready (zone_publication.py ~194-206) and returns Publication, so the diff is discarded. The web uses `change` only in the zone-editor publish review (zones/publish/model.ts). The 'Boundary changed' guard is therefore cheaper than stated: surface validation.zones[].change in the import response. (2) '20 zones means 20 choices' holds only for files without zone ids. A feature that carries a valid current zone_id property is preselected 'same' (identity.ts:27,50-62,86 carriedZoneId); the standard hand-drawn QGIS export does not carry it, and the QGIS docs never mention it. (3) A full re-upload per form revision is the designed contract, not a defect: packages name their forms exactly (deliveryOf comment citing mobile/src/packages/hosted/prepare.ts). A 'rebind' action is feature work, so the category is nearer DESIGN PREFERENCE, with one real hazard: the silent geometry replacement in mixed web-edit and QGIS-upload workflows, whose frequency is unproven. New fact: the upload form-version Select defaults to the current package's version (packages/forms.ts:49-60), so a plain re-upload does not pick the new form. Severity medium is acceptable but low-end.

result.summary:
The collector is careful work. Placement uses a fixed cross with tap-to-jump, 0.5 m nudges and zoom-to-place, plus a live in-zone readout. Recovery reopens the exact map and zone. The download size comes from the server and is checked against the bytes received. "Ready offline" means a re-hashed, verified install. Sign-up and join are short. The flaws are in what the observer sees and touches on a real device, and they cluster in three places.

First, the C3 loop has defects that cost data quality or block a task. On an iPhone, the required multi-line play-event summary is typed blind: the keyboard covers the whole answer panel, and there is no key to dismiss it. A double tap on an auto-advancing answer either clears the answer just given or silently answers the next question; a pure reproduction against janet-test-v1 shows both outcomes. When a draft write fails, the observer is not told, while the Collect status line keeps saying "Draft kept on this device as you answer". If a draft cannot be read, collection is blocked with no card offering a way out.

Second, C4 status words are false where decisions are made. Account and Sign out both say "This version does not upload yet", but uploading is live and signing out pauses it. The Observations tab swaps the whole app for the legacy dark records screen (an operator-verified tablet screenshot shows it). That screen labels waiting records "Held" and uploaded ones "Synced", and its Retry re-sends the same frozen body.

Third, phone layouts were sized for tablets. Map controls are clipped, and the Saved step's only forward action sits below the fold. Separately, in C2, a token refresh silently cancels a running download and briefly shows a downloaded site as "Not downloaded".

Most fixes are small, and several mostly delete code (copy, legacy screen, deps). Nothing here needs a new library or architecture.

The one button that continues the loop is therefore below the fold, with no strip to fall back on. On tablets the button fits, but each observation still costs an extra tap that DESIGN.md removes.
findings.consequence: On phones, every observation needs a scroll and a tap to continue. Map tools that DESIGN promises have a button for every gesture cannot be reached.
findings.smallest_fix: Pin 'Place the next observation' (or 'Inventory … next') outside the ScrollView, as Place, Question and Review already do. On tablet landscape, follow DESIGN.md:232: go straight to Place with the existing 'Last saved on this device' line. Lay the map controls out in two columns when the frame is under about 340 pt, or fold layers, location and expand into the layers menu.
findings.can_delete: The separate Saved step on tablet landscape.
findings.guarantee_to_keep: The save announcement, the success haptic and the status line 'OBS-… saved on this device'. The Upload row wording stays reachable, for example in the scrollable card.
findings.verification_scenario: iPhone 15 simulator in landscape: all six map controls are visible and tappable, and after a save the next-observation button shows without scrolling. iPad landscape: save goes straight to Place with the last-saved line.

findings.title: Every 5 s while online, Account counts and the sign-out warning flash to 'Reading records from this device…' and the Sign out button turns off
findings.platform: iOS and Android, signed in, online, foreground
findings.journey: C4 sign-out
locations: mobile/src/sync/provider.tsx:127-129 (setInterval wake every 5000 ms)
mobile/src/sync/foreground.ts:18-21 (changed() after every drain, even when nothing changed)
mobile/src/storage/use-observations.ts:18-22 (setLoading(true) on every refresh)
mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/account/index.tsx:89-90
mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/account/sign-out.tsx:46-47,80-81,97-98
findings.trigger: Reading Account or Sign out while online with the app in the foreground.
findings.current_behavior: Each idle drain bumps the revision, so useObservations sets loading to true and re-reads the whole table. While it reads, Account replaces its counts with a loading row, and Sign out replaces its warning with a loading state and disables its button. This repeats every 5 s. How long each flash is visible was not measured.
findings.consequence: The counts the observer is reading before deciding to sign out flicker away. A tap on Sign out can land while the button is disabled.
findings.smallest_fix: Have the drain report whether any row changed and call changed() only then. In useObservations, set loading only on the first read for a given key.
findings.can_delete: The unconditional changed() call and the per-tick loading flip.
findings.guarantee_to_keep: Lists still refresh after a save, an acknowledgement or a rejection. Backoff retries keep running.
findings.verification_scenario: Mount SyncProvider online with 0 pending rows and advance fake timers 30 s: listObservations runs once. On a device, watch Account for 30 s online: the counts never change to the loading row.

findings.title: Rotating the device remounts the field map and the step panel, moving the aim back to the zone centre
findings.platform: iOS and Android with orientation set to 'Follow the device' (the default)
findings.journey: C3 Place / Review
locations: mobile/src/features/collect/CollectScreen.tsx:485-503 (map at body>View>View in landscape vs body>View in portrait; panelBlock at child index 1 vs 2)
mobile/src/features/collect/CollectScreen.tsx:64-70 (doc: 'MapLibre stays mounted from the first point to the hundredth')
mobile/src/features/collect/CollectMap.tsx:550-556 (Camera initialViewState placed ?? zone.centre)
mobile/src/features/collect/ReviewStep.tsx:92-94 (local saving state)
findings.trigger: An observer tilts a phone or tablet while aiming or reviewing, and the screen auto-rotates.
findings.current_behavior: React sees a different element type at the map's position, so it unmounts and remounts CollectMap. The camera resets to the placed point or the zone centre at zone zoom, the layer filters reset, and the location watcher restarts. The panel subtree remounts, which also resets Review's saving state. No record or draft is lost.
findings.consequence: The observer's framing is lost mid-aim and has to be found again. Rotating during a save re-enables Save.
findings.smallest_fix: Keep a single tree with the map at a fixed path, using the same wrapper Views in both orientations, and switch flexDirection and size through style only.
findings.can_delete: Nothing.
findings.guarantee_to_keep: The panel stays on the side the layout assigns it, and the 46% map split stays in portrait.
findings.verification_scenario: In an RN test, render CollectScreen and change the window from 390x844 to 844x390: the CollectMap mount effect runs once. On a device, aim, rotate, and the cross stays on the same spot.

findings.title: Collector preferences promised by PRODUCT and DESIGN (preferred hand, haptics, larger text, Dusk) can only be set in dev builds
findings.journey: one-handed reach / outdoor use
locations: mobile/src/ui/preferences.tsx:30-33,75-88 (store and defaults)
mobile/app/(dev)/states.tsx:232 and mobile/app/(dev)/gallery.tsx:257,855,861,881 (the only callers of preferences.set)
mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/account/index.tsx:140-160 (only orientation is settable)
PRODUCT.md:166
DESIGN.md:232 ('panel on the preferred hand's side')
mobile/src/features/collect/CollectScreen.tsx:489 (row-reverse when hand is left)
findings.trigger: A left-handed observer collects on a tablet in landscape.
findings.current_behavior: The side panel is always on the right. There is no release UI to change the hand, haptics, larger answer text or Dusk. OS font scaling is honoured up to 2x (Text.tsx:63), so text size is still reachable.
findings.consequence: A minor reach cost for some observers. The docs promise settings that do not exist.
findings.smallest_fix: Add one Segmented control, 'Panel side: Left · Right', to the existing Account orientation island. Delete the unexposed haptics, larger-text and Dusk preferences and their doc promises, or expose them the same way.
findings.can_delete: Unreachable preference keys and their dev-only setters, if they will not be exposed.
findings.guarantee_to_keep: Day stays the default, and the map palette stays separate from the screen theme.
findings.verification_scenario: On a release build, choose Left in Account, open Collect in landscape, and the panel is on the left.
findings.evidence_needed: Observer feedback on whether panel side matters on tablets.

justified_choices: Crosshair placement (PlaceStep.tsx:82-216, CollectMap.tsx:521-528): a fixed cross with the map moving under it, tap-to-jump that never places by itself, 0.5 m nudge buttons, 'Zoom in to place', a live in-zone readout, and 'Place point here' disabled with a visible reason. This is the right answer to precision with gloves and attention elsewhere, and every gesture has a button.
Validation only at Review, with 'Skip for now' (QuestionStep.tsx:243-250, ReviewStep.tsx:126-133). Required answers never interrupt the stack, and every Review row jumps back to its question.

Saving the record and retiring its draft in one transaction (observation-store.ts:55-77), worded 'Save on this device', with 'Uploaded' shown only after the receipt is validated (queue.ts:9-14, sync-store.ts:80-106).
Offline-first gate: a cached account opens the app without a live session, and 'Sign in to resume uploads' opens sign-in with the email filled in (ResumeUploadsNote.tsx:15-38).

Ready offline from a verified, re-hashed install, and still ready on an older verified map after a newer one is published, with the update offered beside it (versions.ts:94-166,232-240). The download size comes from server archive_bytes and is checked against the received bytes (prepare.ts:24-32).

Unfinished-observation card with exact wording ('Point placed, 3 of 8 answered. Kept on this device.'), Resume, re-download of the pinned map, 'Keep for later', and a confirmed Discard (UnfinishedCard.tsx, recovery.ts).

Sign-up and join friction is low: the OTP checks itself at the sixth digit with a mono cooldown, initials are suggested from the name, the profile saves offline and queues, the join action lifts above the keyboard, and the invitation shows the project before joining (VerifyScreen.tsx:70-99, profile.tsx:82-117, join/index.tsx:131-134).

Brief locks map and form versions visibly ('MAP n · FORM v stay locked', brief.tsx:297-310) and blocks starting a new visit while a resumable observation holds the slot, giving the reason under the button.

Touch sizing: answer tiles at 60 or taller, collector actions at 60, the touch floor at 48, and map controls at 44 with hit slop reaching 48. OS Dynamic Type is honoured up to 2x. State is shown as glyph plus word (StateBadge). Removal is disabled with 'Used by …' reasons.

keep_despite_complex.item: Exact recovery validation (session/ownership.ts:55-93, packages/draft-recovery, recovery.ts)
keep_despite_complex.why: A resumed draft must reopen on the exact map, zone and form version it was started on. Substituting a newer map would reinterpret research data. The many card states (package_missing, package_unavailable, park) are the visible cost of that guarantee.

keep_despite_complex.item: Re-verifying every installed package on catalog load (hosted/installation.ts:71-104)
keep_despite_complex.why: This is what makes 'Ready offline' truthful after an interrupted write or disk corruption. Keep it, but stop re-running it on every token refresh (UXC-06).

keep_despite_complex.item: Per-keystroke draft writes through the serialized databaseWrite queue (QuestionStep.tsx:121-122, storage/database-write.ts)
keep_despite_complex.why: Debouncing would lose the last typed words on a force quit. One expo-sqlite connection needs the FIFO for transaction isolation.

keep_despite_complex.item: The package lease during a collect visit and refusal to remove maps that are referenced (hosted/access.ts, package-catalog.ts:126-160)
keep_despite_complex.why: These stop an observer from removing the map an unfinished observation or an unsent record depends on.

keep_despite_complex.item: The 'Leave? Your draft stays on this device' confirmation, and Android back stepping back through the steps (CollectScreen.tsx:132-172)
keep_despite_complex.why: These make interruption safe and say where the work is. They are cheap and match PRODUCT's honesty rules.

not_covered: Nothing was run on a device or simulator. The layout findings (UXC-01, UXC-07) are computed from contour.json tokens, use-layout.ts and RN 0.86.3 KeyboardAvoidingView source, and still need simulator screenshots.

The only runtime image evidence is the 2026-10-11 Android tablet screenshots. 02-observations.png matches the current records.tsx (unchanged since 2026-10-08), but 03-account.png shows an older Account screen and was not used.
Android keyboard behaviour (softwareKeyboardLayoutMode with edge-to-edge on SDK 57) was not verified, so UXC-01 is claimed for iOS only.
How often real double taps fall at intervals over 160 ms, and how visible the 5 s loading flicker is, were not measured.
VoiceOver/TalkBack order and announcements, Dusk theme contrast, and outdoor legibility in direct sun were not inspected on hardware.
The field guide content, the delete-account flow details, forgot/reset password, and the dev (gallery/states) routes were only skimmed.
Record-loss paths owned by the storage layer (schema reset on SCHEMA_VERSION mismatch, the frozen legacy owner_scope) belong to the records/persistence dimension and are not repeated here.
Web and backend are out of scope for this dimension.

## Native collector journeys: UI/UX assessment (HEAD 9928f53)

Method: I traced code paths and ran one pure-Node reproduction (scratchpad/repro/ux-collector/double-tap.ts). Layout figures are computed from contracts/contour.json tokens, mobile/src/layout/use-layout.ts and the RN 0.86.3 KeyboardAvoidingView source. Runtime image evidence is limited to the operator-verified Android tablet captures from 2026-10-11. Nothing was run on a device or simulator in this pass.

**Outdoor, ergonomics and orientation notes**
- Day is the default, and OS font scaling is honoured up to 2x.
- The legacy Observations screen is dark even in Day.
- On iOS the map is never inside a scroll view, so there is no gesture conflict.
- There is no gesture-only action: back is handled and the collect route has gestureEnabled false.
- Rotation remounts the map (UXC-09).
- The preferred-hand panel side is not settable in release builds (UXC-10).

### Current vs proposed interactions

1. **Typing the play-event summary on a phone**
   - *Current:* tapping the field raises the keyboard over the whole answer panel. The map keeps 46% of the screen. The observer types without seeing the text and cannot reach Continue. The only ways out are the mode strip's "Place" (which enters Adjust point) or X.
   - *Proposed:* while the keyboard is up in Collect (reusing the existing useKeyboardVisible hook), the map and status line collapse by size only, so the question, the field, the counter and Back/Continue sit above the keyboard. Dragging the panel dismisses the keyboard, and Continue moves on. The draft is still written on every keystroke.
2. **Single-choice answers with auto-advance**
   - *Current:* tap "3–5 yrs", and the next question appears 160 ms later in the same grid. A habitual or gloved double tap either clears the age answer or picks "Exploratory" on a play-type question nobody read.
   - *Proposed:* tiles ignore presses for about 400 ms after a question appears, and re-tapping the selected tile in that window does nothing. Auto-advance and deliberate un-choose (after the window) stay.
3. **Saved → next observation**
   - *Current:* after Save, a full card shows the OBS number and four facts. On phones "Place the next observation" is below the fold inside a scroll view. On tablets it is always one more tap.
   - *Proposed:* the next action is pinned at the bottom like every other step. On tablet landscape the save returns straight to Place with "Last saved on this device · OBS-3F2A1B · 11:34", which PlaceStep already renders (DESIGN.md:232). The save is still announced, gives a haptic, and shows "OBS-… saved on this device" in the status line.

### Ranking rationale
1. Blocked or blind core-loop tasks: UXC-01 and UXC-05.
2. Misleading state at the sign-out decision point: UXC-02.
3. Silent research-data error: UXC-03.
4. The status screen leaving the shell with contradictory words: UXC-04.
5. Readiness flicker and a silently cancelled download: UXC-06.
6. Phone layout: UXC-07.
7. Low-impact polish: UXC-08, UXC-09, UXC-10.

The outcome is the same because the panel's window-top is about 506-525 pt against a keyboard top of about 508 pt (QuickType on). The panel is entirely behind the keyboard on SE, 14 and 15 Pro, and at most 14-33 pt shows above it on Pro Max. Without QuickType at most 78 pt shows, which is only the act bar and the eyebrow. Phone landscape leaves about 70 pt above the keyboard, with the field hidden. Even with no keyboard, the 4-row field is mostly below the scroll viewport (about 14 pt visible in portrait), so the observer must scroll first. results.correction: The UI gaps are confirmed. CollectScreen.tsx:431-432 hard-codes 'Draft kept on this device as you answer'. A persistDraft failure only calls setStatus (provider.tsx:125-128), and session.status is rendered only by the legacy components/screen.tsx, never on Collect. useUnfinished() returns null when only unreadableDraft is true, nothing consumes recovered-drafts.ts:63, and openPackage and begin refuse with 'Resume or discard…' (package-actions.ts:65-67, observation-actions.ts:82-84). discardRecovered already clears the unreadable flag, so only the UI is missing. Review rows and links stay pressable while saving (ReviewStep.tsx:171-177,229-232). Not supported: trigger (a). SCHEMA_VERSION was bumped to 5 (10-11) and 6 (10-13), and a version mismatch drops all tables, which is the owner's reset policy. draft-store.ts last changed 10-11 and domain/observation.ts on 10-15 only added sync fields, so there is no evidence the draft schema broke without a bump. An organically unreadable draft is practically unreachable, because the id is a UUID, dates are ISO, and the owner equals the scope. The dead end is therefore a latent trap for a future developer slip, not an ordinary-user path today. Trigger (b) (disk full, authorization removed, ghost-draft race) is real but rare. After a ghost draft, recovery offers Resume or Discard on the next launch, so it is not permanent. Severity downgraded from high to medium. The fix (derive the line from the write result, add a discard card, disable rows while saving) does not ask for migration or compat.

results.checked: Traced auth/provider.tsx:160-195 and session-retention/cached-account (sessionIdentity returns the new session object), the AuthContext value spread, hosted/provider.tsx:50-104 and 127-150, operations.ts dispose, use-site-discovery.ts, me-provider.tsx and HostedPackageIsland.tsx. Searched for guard tests and checked supabase jwt_expiry (3600).
results.correction: The mechanism is confirmed by code reading. A TOKEN_REFRESHED event sets a new session, which recreates api and then PackageOperations. The effect clears downloads and installed, and the cleanup disposes the old operations and aborts the running download. The catch is suppressed because runtime.current() is false after the generation change. Until catalog() re-verifies, HostedPackageIsland shows 'Not downloaded · {size} · needs a connection'. Details: the sites list is not cleared (discovery effect deps are [online, projects] and online stays true), and me-provider.tsx:174 also refetches /v1/me on every refresh. The download is not entirely silent, since the progress bar vanishes and the Download button returns. No test guards session-object stability. Likelihood is low: refresh happens about hourly while foregrounded or at foreground after hours, and colliding with a user-started download needs a fast tap or a long download. The recovery is one re-tap. Severity downgraded from medium to low. The effect duration is unmeasured. Fix keyed on [client, session !== null, userId] is sound. The same session-object churn also restarts SyncProvider's uploader via sessionToken in its deps, which is related but outside this finding.

results.checked: Read CollectMap.tsx (mapStyles frame overflow hidden at :220, controls :247-253 and :762-809, layers menu :254-262), IconButton.tsx, SavedStep.tsx, FactsList.tsx, Island.tsx, CollectScreen layout code, use-layout.ts, PlaceStep.tsx:194-198, DESIGN.md:231-232 and mobile/README.md:21. Ran a layout reproducer (scratchpad/repro/verify-uxc/layout.mjs).
results.correction: Confirmed by arithmetic. The six map controls need 334 pt (6 x 47 + 5 x 8 + 12), and the frame clips them. iPhone 14 portrait has a 284 pt frame, so 'Make the map larger' is hidden. An SE has 230 pt, so layers and expand are hidden. Phone landscape with the strip has about 186 pt, so only zoom ±/frame are fully visible, location is a 9 pt sliver, and layers and expand are hidden. In the collapsed state the expand button, which restores or enlarges the map, is unreachable in portrait. On Saved, the island's lower bound (every fact one line) is 337 pt against panel content of 293 pt (landscape), 314 pt (portrait) and 252 pt (SE). Real facts wrap in the 3/5-width value column, so the island is about 400-450 pt. 'Place the next observation' therefore sits below the fold on every phone. The strip is hidden on Saved, and hardware back only calls leave(). Tablet fits, which is the pilot hardware. The tablet part is a smaller divergence: DESIGN.md:231-232 says Saved becomes a last-saved card in Place, but the code always renders SavedStep. That extra tap also gives a deliberate save confirmation, so it is low and arguably a design preference. The refs are correct (expand button at CollectMap.tsx:807). No iPhone screenshots exist, so the claim is not device-verified.

result.summary:
Both frontends are unusually well built for accessibility. The web Contour primitives wire labels, aria-invalid and aria-describedby once, announce messages through live regions, and restore focus through Radix. They also provide a skip link, route focus, a keyboard-complete zone editor with numeric alternatives, a roving-row table with real links, and a global reduced-motion rule. The native primitives carry roles, state, 48 to 60 pt targets, text-scale caps, Reanimated reduce-motion guards, an announce helper, and a non-gesture placement path (nudge buttons plus "Place point here"). I found no contrast defect after recomputing the full token cross-product, both map palettes and the legacy Nocturne palette. Nothing I found risks record loss.

The material problems sit where the design system stops. First, the release Observations tab is the legacy Nocturne screen, with no heading, 5 stops per record, an 11.5 pt text-only state chip and truncation. Second, the accessibility preferences PRODUCT.md promises (Dusk, larger question text, preferred hand, haptics) can only be changed in dev screens. Third, three native live regions are Android-only, so VoiceOver hears nothing when the cross leaves its zone, while two other places announce twice. Fourth, the native map camera ignores Reduce Motion despite the product's own promise.

Web has three low items. The `g`, `/` and `?` keys violate WCAG 2.1.4. The shortcut dialog documents Approve and Exclude keys that do nothing. The password toggles fail Label in Name.

No axe, keyboard or screen-reader output exists in outputs (the journeys directory is absent). Every spoken-output claim here is code-derived. PLAN.md still lists MOB-18 as todo and the VoiceOver passes as pending, so the largest risk to the pilot is the assistive-technology matrix nobody has run.

justified_choices: Accessibility is built once in the primitives. Contour Field supplies htmlFor, aria-invalid and aria-describedby; Button, IconButton, Switch and Checkbox keep 44 px targets via ::before; Note, Field and the zone editor expose live regions. Screens inherit this, which is why page-level axe plus focused specs is enough.
Radix for Dialog, Menu, Popover, Toast, Tooltip, Checkbox, Switch, RadioGroup and ToggleGroup is the right call. Hand-rolling focus trap, restore and typeahead would be the larger risk.
InkTabs is a nav of links with aria-current, not role=tab. That is the correct pattern for route navigation.
Tables use one tab stop with roving rows, tabIndex -1 on the in-row link, and a real OBS link for screen-reader users (DataTable, useRovingRows, Tr).

The zone editor has non-drag equivalents everywhere: arrow keys on handles, bracket keys, I to insert, a numeric PointsTable, and click-click drawing. This satisfies 2.1.1 and 2.5.7. Midpoint handles are drag-only and aria-hidden, with a keyboard alternative.
Coverage and chart graphics always sit with text: CoverageDots has sr text, CountBars and TypeBars show counts, and the Overview coverage map is a hover aid over a focus-linked table.
Web reduced motion is one global CSS rule, and the map camera uses CSS transitions, so no per-component JS check is needed.
Native has a non-gesture placement path: tap-to-aim, four nudge buttons, a move-to-my-location button and "Place point here" using the map's exact centre, with a live coordinate and zone readout.
Native text uses maxFontSizeMultiplier caps of 1.6, 1.8 or 2 depending on role, and controls use minHeight rather than fixed height. That meets 200 percent resize without letting layouts break.
Native question flow moves screen-reader focus to each question heading on mount (QuestionHeading) and announces place, zone-change and save through one announce helper.
Auth forms allow paste and password managers, use one-time-code autocomplete and noValidate with their own inline errors, and focus the first invalid field. That satisfies 3.3.8 and 1.3.5.

Contrast is enforced from one contract (contracts/contour.json) for both apps. I recomputed the full token cross-product, both map palettes and the legacy Nocturne palette: no pair that is actually used fails. The only sub-4.5 cell is Day attention on ledge (4.40), and ledge is a shadow or hover fill that is never a text background.
Opacity is used only for disabled controls on web, which WCAG exempts; no text is dimmed with an opacity modifier.

keep_despite_complex.item: web/src/features/shell/ShellProvider.tsx useReturningFocus, Switchers.tsx useNavigatingMenu and the onCloseAutoFocus overrides
keep_despite_complex.why: They look like over-engineering but fix the known Radix conflict where a menu hands focus back to its trigger after RouteFocus has moved it to the new page title. Removing them breaks focus after palette and menu navigation.

keep_despite_complex.item: mobile/src/ui/Note.tsx and StatusLine.tsx iOS-only announce effects beside accessibilityLiveRegion
keep_despite_complex.why: React Native's accessibilityLiveRegion is Android-only in the installed 0.86.3, so the iOS effect is the only way these messages are spoken on iOS. Extend the pattern (A11Y-03); do not remove it.

keep_despite_complex.item: mobile/src/ui/TabDock.tsx hand-written accessibilityLabel with ", tab, N of M"
keep_despite_complex.why: RN iOS maps role tab to no trait (RCTViewManager.m:105), so without it VoiceOver does not say "tab" or the position. Android may duplicate it; confirm at runtime before changing.

keep_despite_complex.item: mobile/src/ui/Button.tsx hidden busy-label ghost with accessibilityElementsHidden
keep_despite_complex.why: It keeps width stable while busy without letting a screen reader read both labels.

keep_despite_complex.item: web MapFrame data-map-keys and data-map-overlay protocol, and the Tr onClick plus real in-row link pattern
keep_despite_complex.why: They let a focused handle own the arrow keys without the frame panning, and let keyboard and screen-reader users reach the same destination as the click without a second tab stop.

keep_despite_complex.item: web/src/components/contour/Table.tsx conditional tabIndex and region role on a scrolling table
keep_despite_complex.why: Only a table that actually overflows becomes a keyboard stop, so arrow keys can scroll it without adding dead tab stops everywhere.

not_covered: Runtime assistive-technology output: no VoiceOver, TalkBack, NVDA, JAWS or Voice Control run exists, and the journeys, e2e and native evidence directories are absent. Every spoken-output statement here is derived from code and installed framework sources.
Axe results: web/e2e honesty scans and the zones specimen runs were not executed. Their configuration was read, not their output.
Hardware-keyboard, Full Keyboard Access and Switch Control behaviour on native; only TextInput draws a focus ring.
Forced-colors or Windows High Contrast on web (no forced-colors rules exist, and sliding-pill backgrounds would vanish) and OS Increase Contrast or Bold Text on native.
Actual 320 px reflow, 1.4.12 text-spacing overrides, 400 percent zoom, and 200 percent dynamic type clipping on native; only code-level fixed-height checks were done.
VoiceOver and TalkBack reading order on the collect screen, MapLibre's own accessibility tree, and whether the Map accessibilityLabel prop reaches the native view.
Legal and marketing page content, the OTP and invitation email templates, printed or PDF report accessibility, and QGIS outputs.
The generated mobile/ios and mobile/android projects, and native dev galleries (dev-only).
The designs that PLAN.md says are not committed, so design-versus-build comparisons were not made.
